Avasant Generative AI Services 2025 RadarViewTM Survey
Congratulations!  
In recognition of your organization’s position as a key generative AI (Gen AI) services provider, Avasant invites you to provide input for our upcoming RadarView assessment in this space.    
Avasant Generative AI Services 2024 RadarView™ has received great traction from enterprises and providers for insights on the generative AI (Gen AI) services capabilities and the provider landscape. This survey will support data collection for the annual refresh of the 2025 report.
RadarView is a pioneering analytical assessment in key digital technology domains that leverages Avasant’s proprietary Digital Maturity Framework to evaluate leading service providers based on company disclosures and market checks. These assessments will be released to help global organizations identify, assess, and down-select leading service providers to support their digital transformation initiatives. Service providers can also leverage and license these assessments to enhance their public credentials and promote their capabilities to potential clients.
   
You can find more details on the RadarView program here.
   
We invite you to use the online survey to provide input about your Gen AI services to our industry analysts. The survey responses will augment the assessment by Avasant using publicly available information and independent market checks.
ABOUT THE SURVEY
The Generative AI Services 2025 RadarView Survey comprises 21 questions covering the following aspects:
Practice overview and capabilities
Client and project details
Industry ecosystem overview
Strategy and investment plans

Clients are increasingly introducing contractual clauses to mitigate Gen AI risks related to data privacy, governance, and accountability. These include:
Content Accountability: Mandating factuality validation, prompt engineering reviews, red teaming, and model testing to reduce hallucinations and bias in AI-generated content.
Privacy & IP Compliance: Clauses require strict handling of user data during tagging, annotation, and transcription, along with copyright/IP checks and privacy violation reviews.
Human-in-the-Loop Governance: Ensuring human oversight for content moderation, policy enforcement, sentiment analysis, and sensitive data processing.
Model Governance & Explainability: Stipulations for continuous benchmarking, validation, side-by-side evaluations, and model monitoring for transparency and fairness.
Platform Integrity & Safety: Requirements for AI-supported user authentication, identity theft prevention, and platform safety through moderation and community management.
Regulatory Compliance: Legal clauses for jurisdiction-based policy design, regulatory response handling, and legal removal processes.
Audit & Monitoring: Requiring audit logs, model performance tracking, and periodic reviews to ensure responsible AI use.
Scope Control: Limiting AI deployment to approved use cases with clear usage boundaries and content restrictions.
These align with Firstsource’s Trust & Safety and Gen AI services, enabling clients to meet evolving governance and compliance standards effectively.

Audit & Monitoring: Requiring audit logs, model performance tracking, and periodic reviews to ensure responsible AI use.
Scope Control: Limiting AI deployment to approved use cases with clear usage boundaries and content restrictions.

Avasant Applied AI Services 2026 RadarView™ Survey
Congratulations!  
In recognition of your organization’s position as a key AI and automation services provider, Avasant invites you to provide inputs for our upcoming Applied AI Services 2026 RadarView assessment.

Applied AI Services 2024 RadarView and Applied AI Services 2025 RadarView have received great traction from enterprises and providers for their insights about the applied AI market and the provider landscape they contain. This survey will support data collection for the annual refresh of the 2026 report.

RadarView is a pioneering analytical assessment in key digital technology domains that leverages Avasant’s proprietary Digital Maturity Framework to evaluate leading service providers based on company disclosures and market checks. These assessments will be released to help global organizations identify, assess, and down-select leading service providers in nascent technology areas. Service providers can also license these assessments to enhance their public credentials and promote their capabilities to potential clients.
​
​You can find more details on RadarView here.
We invite you to use the online survey below to provide input about you Applied AI practice and capabilities to our industry analysts. The survey responses will augment the assessment by Avasant using publicly available information and market checks.
About the survey
The Applied AI RadarView Survey comprises 31 questions across six key sections:   	
Practice overview and capabilities
Client and project details
Human capital overview
Industry ecosystem overview
Strategy and investment plans

​Please complete the survey and submit your responses before July 20, 2026, 5 p.m. Pacific Time.
The survey will become inactive after that, and no modification or update will be possible.
The survey allows for stop-start completion through an automatic save feature. There is no separate “Save” button.
There are prescribed word limits in descriptive questions, and we recommend brief and self-explanatory responses. ​Avasant does not guarantee that the submission of this survey automatically qualifies or disqualifies any service provider from the subsequent stages of the RadarView assessment.
For any clarifications on the survey, please reach out to abhisekh.satapathy@avasant.com.

Use case: Mortgage Language Model (Domain LLM) 
Firstsource developed a domain-specific Mortgage Language Model to support underwriting, servicing, and collections workflows where general LLMs lacked domain depth. 
Why domain LLM (instead of foundational LLM): 
Need for deep domain understanding of mortgage terminology and workflows 
Requirement for high accuracy in regulated financial processes 
Need for data privacy and controlled enterprise training environments 
Demand for explainability and auditability in decision-making workflows 
Impact: 
~40% faster decision-making (300+ mortgage-specific concepts embedded) 
>99% accuracy on compliance-critical decisions; ~15% reduction in interpretation errors 
Full auditability and regulatory traceability

Needed high accuracy in complex, semi-structured medical forms with adaptability to new formats and compliance-critical workflows.

Impact: 
~98.5%+ HCFA accuracy; significant uplift over zero-shot baselines 
6–8 hours fine-tuning vs multi-week traditional retraining 
Eliminated OCR errors with single-pass structured output

AI in Healthcare Payor
What is your organization's AI strategy for the Healthcare Payor vertical — including your AI vision, target use cases, and 18-month roadmap? (Describe your overarching AI vision for the Healthcare Payor vertical, your top 3–5 priority use cases, and key milestones planned over the next 6, 12, and 18 months.)
Firstsource’s AI strategy for the healthcare payer vertical is anchored in Intelligence that Operates — our commitment to encode deep payer domain expertise into AI that does not merely advise or automate, but actively operates work end-to-end with accountability. This strategy is delivered through Kairos, our operating system for AI-native operations, which is the dominant architectural and operating construct across our payer AI portfolio. Around Kairos, we combine payer platforms, AI partners, process intelligence tools, and reusable accelerators so that every deployment compounds operational knowledge rather than remaining a standalone point solution. The response that follows sets out our AI vision for the payer vertical, our priority use cases for the next eighteen months, the engagement model through which we deliver, the milestones we are targeting over the next 6, 12, and 18 months, and the governance and outcome-accountability principles that underpin the model.
AI Vision for the Healthcare Payor Vertical
Firstsource’s AI vision for healthcare payers is to operate the payer value chain — claims, customer service, member engagement, care management, provider data and network management, payment integrity, and quality and regulatory workflows — as an AI-native operating model in which AI agents, copilots, and human associates work as one accountable workforce. This vision is expressly delivered through Kairos, which serves as the dominant operating environment for payer workflows by combining payer-specific skills and guardrails, contextual intelligence drawn from client systems and domain knowledge, and operational signals from process, task, document, and conversation intelligence. The result is a payer operating model where regulatory exposure, member experience, medical-cost performance, and workforce productivity improve together rather than in isolation, and where every new deployment strengthens the Kairos operating layer for subsequent payer engagements.
Top Priority Use Cases (next 18 months)
Agentic claims adjudication and Late Payment Interest (LPI) prevention — combining Claims Agentic AI workflows, propensity models, and operational sensors to identify high-risk claims early, prioritize work intelligently, and reduce late-payment exposure.
Sympraxis® Communication Hub expansion across appeals and grievances, prior authorization, and provider correspondence — converting unstructured payer intake into structured downstream action with automated classification, summarization, extraction, routing, and case creation.
Member experience transformation through Member Outreach, Benefit Inquiry, conversational AI, QA/QC, and customer-service agentic workflows — improving response times, digital containment, and service quality across member and provider interactions.
Provider data and contract intelligence — AI-powered classification, extraction, validation, and workflow support across provider onboarding, contracting, directory quality, and network administration.
Risk adjustment, quality, and care-gap optimization — through Risk Adjustment Copilot, Care Gap Reviews, Prior Authorization Copilot, and related clinical-document summarization workflows to improve accuracy, timeliness, and quality outcomes.
Payment integrity at scale — combining Claims & Payment Integrity Copilot, Integrity 360, and process intelligence to improve audit productivity, reduce leakage, and strengthen recovery performance.
Engagement Model
Firstsource delivers every engagement through a structured three-stage motion — Transform, Implement, and Operate — as a single continuous programme under one contract, supported by three commercial entry points calibrated to client ambition and readiness. Level 1 Discover is a four-week, fixed-fee AI and operations maturity assessment that benchmarks the payer against vertical peers and produces a board-ready transformation business case. Level 2 Explore and Expand is a 90-day, outcomes-linked deployment that puts the first AI-powered payer process into production within 90 days. Level 3 Propel is a 12-month retainer with an outcomes bonus, supported by a named Kairos Lead accountable for quarterly board-level outcome reviews and continuous optimisation across the deployed footprint.
6-Month Milestones
Expand Kairos-enabled payer workflows across additional claims, service, and intake use cases, with selected skills progressing to higher-autonomy tiers under structured human oversight.
Scale healthcare-payer-focused AI and technology lab activity around claims, intake, service, and clinical workflow use cases, including co-innovation with anchor clients.
Advance production deployment of LPI, communication-hub, and provider-data intelligence use cases with stronger traceability, monitoring, and governance instrumentation.
12-Month Milestones
Launch additional Kairos-enabled payer skills and benchmarks across claims, payment integrity, service, and care workflows to support more repeatable transformation starts.
Scale Agentic AI Studio, Claims Agentic AI Workflow, Customer Service Agentic AI Workflow, QA/QC Copilot, and training copilots from pilot and anchor deployments into broader production usage.
Advance prior-authorization, clinical summarization, risk-adjustment, and care-gap workflows under structured human oversight, aligned to payer policy and regulatory requirements.
Extend payer interoperability and workflow integration to support broader digital intake, service, and adjudication use cases at scale.
18-Month Milestones
Scale Kairos-enabled agentic payer operations across a broader portfolio of outcome-linked engagements, with named delivery leaders accountable for measurable improvement.
Further productize AI-led payment integrity, quality, and service offerings using reusable Kairos skills, operational context, and payer-specific accelerators.
Expand the Kairos ecosystem across hyperscalers, specialist AI partners, BPaaS platforms, and system-integration partnerships to support greater deployment choice and scale.
Governance and Outcome Accountability
Governance is architected into the operating model rather than bolted on after the fact. Our Progressive Trust approach calibrates AI autonomy through staged human oversight, with skills progressing only after evidence of stable performance, quality, and compliance. Domain-specific guardrails, access controls, traceability, and responsible-AI review are embedded into Kairos-enabled workflows, and outcome accountability is expressed commercially through fixed-fee, outcome-linked, and value-oriented models depending on client maturity and scope. The combination — Intelligence that Operates, delivered through Kairos, governed through progressive oversight, and tied to measurable business outcomes — is how Firstsource differentiates as a payer digital services partner.

Hybrid by design. Firstsource builds the layers of the AI stack that compound into proprietary, payer-specific IP; partners on the layers where hyperscaler and platform economics favor scale; and licenses best-in-class specialist solutions where domain-specific platforms are already strong reference points. Operating Model — Kairos-led Build, Partner, and License

Licensed components — best-in-class specialist platforms that extend the Kairos operating environment in domains where niche vendors hold the strongest reference capability:

Foundational Models in Production for Payer Clients
Model selection is made per skill, per client, and per deployment environment rather than as a single firm-wide standard, allowing us to align with each client’s preferred cloud, regulatory posture, and cost-performance requirements. In practice, we leverage enterprise AI ecosystems across Microsoft Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, and Meta/Llama-based ecosystems, alongside specialist AI platforms and open-source tooling where appropriate. Kairos is intentionally model-agnostic: payer skills, context, orchestration, and governance persist independently of whichever foundation model is selected for a given workflow.
Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service — GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, and GPT-4 Turbo — used for the majority of Generative AI workloads under our enterprise Microsoft partnership.
Amazon Web Services Bedrock — Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Claude 3.5 Haiku, and Meta Llama 3 — used for client environments standardised on AWS.
Google Vertex AI — Gemini 1.5 Pro and Gemini 1.5 Flash — used for select engagements, including clients standardised on Google Cloud.
Open-weight models such as Meta Llama 3 and Mistral — fine-tuned and hosted privately for narrowly scoped, high-volume tasks where unit hosting cost is the binding constraint and the workload is well-defined enough to specialise the model.
Specialty Models and AI Capabilities
Beyond foundational language models, we deploy specialty models and frameworks for targeted capabilities such as semantic retrieval, transcription, intent classification, propensity scoring, summarization, document understanding, and workflow orchestration. These are selected according to the use case — for example, payer-document retrieval, contact-center interaction analysis, claims risk scoring, or process-intelligence monitoring — and are composed through Kairos so that domain-specific logic and contextual intelligence remain stable even when underlying models or tools evolve.
Cohere Embed and the OpenAI embedding family for semantic retrieval over payer documents, SOPs, contracts, and clinical guidelines.
OpenAI Whisper for batch transcription; AssemblyAI for real-time transcription in contact-centre and clinical-triage interactions.
XGBoost and DistilBERT for in-house risk-propensity, intent-classification, and Late Payment Interest (LPI) propensity-scoring models.
LangGraph and Temporal for durable agent orchestration; MCP (Model Context Protocol) for structured tool and data integration.
Rationale — Kairos as the durable, model-agnostic operating layer
Kairos is deliberately model-agnostic. Following our first agentic design tenet — separate Brain, Hands, and Memory — the reasoning layer (Brain), the skill library (Hands), and the durable context (Memory) are kept as independent, loosely coupled components. The Domain Harness, part of the Kairos Architecture, the Intelligent Context Framework, and the skill libraries persist as Firstsource and client IP regardless of which foundational model provides reasoning at any given moment. We are able to swap models skill-by-skill, client-by-client, and region-by-region without rewriting our domain assets, which protects clients from vendor lock-in, foundational-model pricing volatility, and the accelerating pace of model deprecation. Equally important, it ensures that 25+ years of payer domain expertise continues to compound inside the durable layers Firstsource owns and operates, rather than inside the foundational models we rent.

Integration surface
Our agents do not operate in isolation. Agents read from and write to these systems through secure, governed APIs, ensuring that every action is traceable back to the calling agent and the underlying decision logic.
How we govern autonomy
Agentic AI introduces operational risk that copilots and traditional automation do not. Firstsource addresses this risk through three reinforcing layers of governance.
Principle-based governance. Every deployment is evaluated against eight standards — fairness, AI for good, regulatory compliance, accountability, interpretability, privacy and security, inclusiveness, and reliability. These principles translate into concrete acceptance criteria during model validation and into ongoing monitoring once a workflow is deployed.
Autonomy calibration through Progressive Trust. We do not deploy agents at full autonomy from day one. Every workflow begins under Human-in-the-Loop review at every decision, where the agent's output is approved or corrected before any downstream action is taken. As we accumulate evidence of sustained accuracy on a defined task, we graduate the workflow to Human-on-the-Loop, where the human supervises the agent's actions rather than approving each one. Only low-risk, high-confidence task domains progress to Human-above-the-Loop autonomy, and continuous post-hoc audit is maintained even at that level. This progression keeps our risk posture conservative and allows us to demonstrate compliance to regulators and clients alike.
Platform-level technical control. Lyzr provides reflection-based validation, groundedness checks against enterprise knowledge sources, fairness and bias safeguards, toxicity monitoring, automated PII detection and redaction, and token-level audit logs. Opus enforces compliance tracking and embeds explicit human review checkpoints at every workflow step.
Underlying all of this, our infrastructure is certified to ISO 27001, HITRUST, SOC 2 Type 2, and HIPAA. Business Associate Agreements cover every client engagement. A 24/7 Security Operations Center, operated in partnership with PwC on Microsoft Sentinel SIEM, monitors continuously across our environment.

Sympraxis ingests provider and member documents from multiple intake channels (mail, fax, portals, EDI), automates document classification, data extraction, summarization, and case creation through GenAI and OCR/ICR pipelines, and routes work into downstream queues. While Sympraxis itself is intelligent document processing rather than fully autonomous agentic execution, it provides the agentic triage and routing layer on which our downstream autonomous agents operate.

Responsible AI capabilities
Compliance with CMS and HIPAA for AI-driven decisions
For AI-driven decisions in payor environments, regulatory compliance is enforced at three layers: technical control, process control, and human authority.
At the technical layer, our infrastructure is certified to HIPAA, HITRUST CSF, SOC 2 Type 2, and ISO 27001, with Business Associate Agreements covering every payor client engagement. Encryption, access controls, audit logging, and breach notification capabilities meet or exceed HIPAA Security Rule requirements. For AI-specific governance, our control environment is aligned to ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management systems) and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.
At the process layer, we map each AI deployment to applicable federal and state regulations during use-case design. For prior authorization deployments specifically, our agents are designed to comply with the CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final Rule (CMS-0057-F), including the timeliness mandates that took effect in January 2026. For deployments touching Medicare Advantage coverage decisions, our agents are configured in line with CMS guidance that algorithms and AI models cannot be the sole basis for a coverage or medical necessity determination clinical reviewers retain authority, and AI outputs serve as decision support, not decision-making. Section 1557 non-discrimination requirements are reflected in our fairness testing protocols, and 21st Century Cures Act information-blocking obligations are addressed in our data access patterns.
At the human authority layer, every AI-driven decision that affects a member or provider coverage, payment, authorization, or appeals outcome — is either reviewed by a qualified human or governed by a Progressive Trust autonomy level that has been explicitly authorized by the client. Clinical decisions remain the responsibility of credentialed clinicians; payment decisions remain the responsibility of qualified claims professionals. AI accelerates and informs these decisions; it does not replace the regulated decision-maker.
Firstsource treats Responsible AI not as a policy document, but as an operating model. Every agentic and generative AI deployment in our payor portfolio operates under the same eight-principle Kairos Responsible AI framework, the same Progressive Trust calibration, the same platform-level controls, and the same multi-tier governance ownership. Regulatory compliance with CMS, HIPAA, Section 1557, and state-level requirements are enforced through technical certification, process design, and human authority working together. As regulatory expectations around AI in healthcare continue to evolve, including the CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final Rule and emerging state-level AI accountability legislation, our governance framework is designed to absorb new requirements without disrupting client operations.

What is your AI governance framework for payor clients — including model validation, drift monitoring, audit trails, and rollback mechanisms? (Describe the governance components in place — such as model validation, drift monitoring, audit trails, rollback mechanisms, and governance boards — including the frequency of each activity, who approves models before deployment, how incidents are escalated, and what the rollback SLA is.)
Our AI governance framework for payor clients is designed to make Intelligence that Operates safe, auditable, and production-ready. Kairos acts as the governance operating layer as much as the orchestration layer: it enforces deployment gates, captures traceability, calibrates autonomy through Progressive Trust, and supports rollback when performance or policy conditions require it.
Core governance components
Model validation: design review, data-lineage review, offline validation, fairness and error analysis, and workflow acceptance testing before pilot or production.
Autonomy calibration: workflows begin under Human-in-the-Loop oversight and graduate only after sustained performance and explicit sign-off.
Drift monitoring: production monitoring covers accuracy, confidence, throughput, exceptions, fairness signals, and input-distribution drift.
Audit trails: model version, workflow version, data access, decision path, overrides, and downstream actions are recorded and searchable.
Rollback and incident response: material failures trigger containment, root-cause analysis, rollback to a known-good version or manual fallback, client notification, and documented remediation.
Validation occurs before every material release. Monitoring is typically weekly during stabilization and monthly or quarterly in steady state, depending on risk. Rollback SLAs are defined by use case; for higher-risk workflows, fallback to a prior model or manual mode is typically targeted within hours, not days.
How do you manage data privacy and security when training or fine-tuning AI models on payor member/claims data? (Describe the data privacy controls in place — such as de-identification, synthetic data generation, federated learning, or HIPAA BAAs — including where payor data is stored during training, who has access, how consent and authorization are managed, and any certifications or third-party audits that validate your data privacy posture.)
When training or fine-tuning AI on payor member or claims data, we apply a privacy-by-design model. The starting principle is to use the least sensitive data required, prefer retrieval-grounded or configuration-driven approaches where possible, and where training is required, apply de-identification, access control, contractual controls, and auditable operating procedures throughout the lifecycle. This is managed through Kairos so that data handling, model promotion, and runtime usage remain governed under one operating model.
Core controls
De-identification: Safe Harbor or Expert Determination methods where appropriate; for many GenAI workflows we prefer RAG over broad fine-tuning on raw PHI.
Data minimization: only the minimum fields needed for the task are used; retention is defined by client contract and governance policy.
Logical segregation and access control: client data is segregated by client and environment; access is least-privilege, role-based, logged, and reviewed.
Secure storage and transfer: encryption in transit and at rest, governed environments, and auditable access pathways.
Contractual controls: BAAs, client-approved processing terms, audit rights, and incident-response obligations.
Training and tuning datasets are stored in client-approved cloud or enterprise environments aligned to regulatory and residency requirements. Access is restricted to authorized delivery, engineering, data science, and governance personnel on a documented need-to-know basis, and all access is auditable.

We maintain governance processes designed for the possibility of model failure, performance degradation, or bias drift in payor environments. As a matter of confidentiality, we do not disclose client-specific incidents publicly; however, where a material issue is detected, our response is consistent: contain the issue, reduce autonomy or revert to manual fallback, investigate root cause, remediate, disclose to the client as required, and only then restore normal operation. This response is built into Kairos and reinforced through Progressive Trust governance.
Standard response pattern
Detection: alerts, override patterns, QA sampling, fairness checks, client feedback, or exception spikes.
Containment: move to Human-in-the-Loop or manual fallback.
Root-cause analysis: determine whether the issue arose from data drift, policy change, prompt or retrieval error, model degradation, or workflow integration error.
Remediation: recalibration, data refresh, policy update, routing change, model rollback, or additional human review gates.
Disclosure and learning: notify the client per governance terms and feed the lessons back into validation thresholds, monitoring, and deployment standards.

AI in Healthcare Payor
What is your organization's AI strategy for the Healthcare Payor vertical — including your AI vision, target use cases, and 18-month roadmap? (Describe your overarching AI vision for the Healthcare Payor vertical, your top 3–5 priority use cases, and key milestones planned over the next 6, 12, and 18 months.)
Firstsource’s AI strategy for the healthcare payer vertical is anchored in Intelligence that Operates — our commitment to encode deep payer domain expertise into AI that does not merely advise or automate, but actively operates work end-to-end with accountability. This strategy is delivered through Kairos, our operating system for AI-native operations, which is the dominant architectural and operating construct across our payer AI portfolio. Around Kairos, we combine payer platforms, AI partners, process intelligence tools, and reusable accelerators so that every deployment compounds operational knowledge rather than remaining a standalone point solution. The response that follows sets out our AI vision for the payer vertical, our priority use cases for the next eighteen months, the engagement model through which we deliver, the milestones we are targeting over the next 6, 12, and 18 months, and the governance and outcome-accountability principles that underpin the model.
AI Vision for the Healthcare Payor Vertical
Firstsource’s AI vision for healthcare payers is to operate the payer value chain — claims, customer service, member engagement, care management, provider data and network management, payment integrity, and quality and regulatory workflows — as an AI-native operating model in which AI agents, copilots, and human associates work as one accountable workforce. This vision is expressly delivered through Kairos, which serves as the dominant operating environment for payer workflows by combining payer-specific skills and guardrails, contextual intelligence drawn from client systems and domain knowledge, and operational signals from process, task, document, and conversation intelligence. The result is a payer operating model where regulatory exposure, member experience, medical-cost performance, and workforce productivity improve together rather than in isolation, and where every new deployment strengthens the Kairos operating layer for subsequent payer engagements.
Top Priority Use Cases (next 18 months)
Agentic claims adjudication and Late Payment Interest (LPI) prevention — combining Claims Agentic AI workflows, propensity models, and operational sensors to identify high-risk claims early, prioritize work intelligently, and reduce late-payment exposure.
Sympraxis® Communication Hub expansion across appeals and grievances, prior authorization, and provider correspondence — converting unstructured payer intake into structured downstream action with automated classification, summarization, extraction, routing, and case creation.
Member experience transformation through Member Outreach, Benefit Inquiry, conversational AI, QA/QC, and customer-service agentic workflows — improving response times, digital containment, and service quality across member and provider interactions.
Provider data and contract intelligence — AI-powered classification, extraction, validation, and workflow support across provider onboarding, contracting, directory quality, and network administration.
Risk adjustment, quality, and care-gap optimization — through Risk Adjustment Copilot, Care Gap Reviews, Prior Authorization Copilot, and related clinical-document summarization workflows to improve accuracy, timeliness, and quality outcomes.
Payment integrity at scale — combining Claims & Payment Integrity Copilot, Integrity 360, and process intelligence to improve audit productivity, reduce leakage, and strengthen recovery performance.
Engagement Model
Firstsource delivers every engagement through a structured three-stage motion — Transform, Implement, and Operate — as a single continuous programme under one contract, supported by three commercial entry points calibrated to client ambition and readiness. Level 1 Discover is a four-week, fixed-fee AI and operations maturity assessment that benchmarks the payer against vertical peers and produces a board-ready transformation business case. Level 2 Explore and Expand is a 90-day, outcomes-linked deployment that puts the first AI-powered payer process into production within 90 days. Level 3 Propel is a 12-month retainer with an outcomes bonus, supported by a named Kairos Lead accountable for quarterly board-level outcome reviews and continuous optimisation across the deployed footprint.
6-Month Milestones
Expand Kairos-enabled payer workflows across additional claims, service, and intake use cases, with selected skills progressing to higher-autonomy tiers under structured human oversight.
Scale healthcare-payer-focused AI and technology lab activity around claims, intake, service, and clinical workflow use cases, including co-innovation with anchor clients.
Advance production deployment of LPI, communication-hub, and provider-data intelligence use cases with stronger traceability, monitoring, and governance instrumentation.
12-Month Milestones
Launch additional Kairos-enabled payer skills and benchmarks across claims, payment integrity, service, and care workflows to support more repeatable transformation starts.
Scale Agentic AI Studio, Claims Agentic AI Workflow, Customer Service Agentic AI Workflow, QA/QC Copilot, and training copilots from pilot and anchor deployments into broader production usage.
Advance prior-authorization, clinical summarization, risk-adjustment, and care-gap workflows under structured human oversight, aligned to payer policy and regulatory requirements.
Extend payer interoperability and workflow integration to support broader digital intake, service, and adjudication use cases at scale.
18-Month Milestones
Scale Kairos-enabled agentic payer operations across a broader portfolio of outcome-linked engagements, with named delivery leaders accountable for measurable improvement.
Further productize AI-led payment integrity, quality, and service offerings using reusable Kairos skills, operational context, and payer-specific accelerators.
Expand the Kairos ecosystem across hyperscalers, specialist AI partners, BPaaS platforms, and system-integration partnerships to support greater deployment choice and scale.
Governance and Outcome Accountability
Governance is architected into the operating model rather than bolted on after the fact. Our Progressive Trust approach calibrates AI autonomy through staged human oversight, with skills progressing only after evidence of stable performance, quality, and compliance. Domain-specific guardrails, access controls, traceability, and responsible-AI review are embedded into Kairos-enabled workflows, and outcome accountability is expressed commercially through fixed-fee, outcome-linked, and value-oriented models depending on client maturity and scope. The combination — Intelligence that Operates, delivered through Kairos, governed through progressive oversight, and tied to measurable business outcomes — is how Firstsource differentiates as a payer digital services partner.

Hybrid by design. Firstsource builds the layers of the AI stack that compound into proprietary, payer-specific IP; partners on the layers where hyperscaler and platform economics favor scale; and licenses best-in-class specialist solutions where domain-specific platforms are already strong reference points. This is a deliberate architectural choice that protects client value over time, and within this model Kairos serves as the operating environment that ties proprietary skills, contextual intelligence, orchestration, and governance together.
Operating Model — Kairos-led Build, Partner, and License
Built components — the durable, payer-specific IP that compounds with every engagement and is orchestrated through Kairos as the dominant operating system for payer AI:
The Domain Harness part of the Kairos architecture— encoding 25+ years of payer expertise as executable skills, playbooks, and guardrails.
The Intelligent Context Framework (ICF) — capturing canonical member, provider, claim, contract, and clinical entity context, with Decision Traces preserving the full causal chain of every AI-assisted decision.
Operations Intelligence sensors — Process Mining, Object-Centric Process Mining, Task Mining, Conversation Intelligence, Knowledge Mining, and Document Intelligence — surfacing in-flight signal across payer operations.
A growing portfolio of proprietary copilots and agentic workflows, including the Claims and Payment Integrity Copilot, the Claims Agentic AI Workflow, the Customer Service Agentic AI Workflow, the Prior Authorisation Copilot, the Risk Adjustment Copilot, the Care Gap Reviews Copilot, the SARA Instructional Design Copilot, and the WFM Real-Time Adherence Copilot.
Partnered components — the scale layers that plug into Kairos where hyperscaler and platform economics favor broader ecosystem leverage:
Foundational large language models, accessed through hyperscaler enterprise agreements rather than direct model contracts — detailed in the section that follows.
Vector databases, embedding stores, and retrieval infrastructure (Pinecone, OpenSearch, Neo4j).
Hyperscaler infrastructure — Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services, and Google Cloud — chosen per engagement to align with the client's preferred cloud.
Licensed components — best-in-class specialist platforms that extend the Kairos operating environment in domains where niche vendors hold the strongest reference capability:
Celonis for Object-Centric Process Mining, Soroco Scout for Task Mining, and HiLabs for healthcare-specific data quality.
Lyzr Agent Studio and Opus Applied AI for agentic workflow orchestration accelerators.
Codoxo and Edifecs for encounter and fraud-waste-abuse submission workflows; Andros for provider credentialing; Simplify Healthcare for network management; Ribbon Health and Perspecta for provider directory data quality.
Foundational Models in Production for Payer Clients
Model selection is made per skill, per client, and per deployment environment rather than as a single firm-wide standard, allowing us to align with each client’s preferred cloud, regulatory posture, and cost-performance requirements. In practice, we leverage enterprise AI ecosystems across Microsoft Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, and Meta/Llama-based ecosystems, alongside specialist AI platforms and open-source tooling where appropriate. Kairos is intentionally model-agnostic: payer skills, context, orchestration, and governance persist independently of whichever foundation model is selected for a given workflow.
Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service — GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, and GPT-4 Turbo — used for the majority of Generative AI workloads under our enterprise Microsoft partnership.
Amazon Web Services Bedrock — Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Claude 3.5 Haiku, and Meta Llama 3 — used for client environments standardised on AWS.
Google Vertex AI — Gemini 1.5 Pro and Gemini 1.5 Flash — used for select engagements, including clients standardised on Google Cloud.
Open-weight models such as Meta Llama 3 and Mistral — fine-tuned and hosted privately for narrowly scoped, high-volume tasks where unit hosting cost is the binding constraint and the workload is well-defined enough to specialise the model.
Specialty Models and AI Capabilities
Beyond foundational language models, we deploy specialty models and frameworks for targeted capabilities such as semantic retrieval, transcription, intent classification, propensity scoring, summarization, document understanding, and workflow orchestration. These are selected according to the use case — for example, payer-document retrieval, contact-center interaction analysis, claims risk scoring, or process-intelligence monitoring — and are composed through Kairos so that domain-specific logic and contextual intelligence remain stable even when underlying models or tools evolve.
Cohere Embed and the OpenAI embedding family for semantic retrieval over payer documents, SOPs, contracts, and clinical guidelines.
OpenAI Whisper for batch transcription; AssemblyAI for real-time transcription in contact-centre and clinical-triage interactions.
XGBoost and DistilBERT for in-house risk-propensity, intent-classification, and Late Payment Interest (LPI) propensity-scoring models.
LangGraph and Temporal for durable agent orchestration; MCP (Model Context Protocol) for structured tool and data integration.
Rationale — Kairos as the durable, model-agnostic operating layer
Kairos is deliberately model-agnostic. Following our first agentic design tenet — separate Brain, Hands, and Memory — the reasoning layer (Brain), the skill library (Hands), and the durable context (Memory) are kept as independent, loosely coupled components. The Domain Harness, part of the Kairos Architecture, the Intelligent Context Framework, and the skill libraries persist as Firstsource and client IP regardless of which foundational model provides reasoning at any given moment. We are able to swap models skill-by-skill, client-by-client, and region-by-region without rewriting our domain assets, which protects clients from vendor lock-in, foundational-model pricing volatility, and the accelerating pace of model deprecation. Equally important, it ensures that 25+ years of payer domain expertise continues to compound inside the durable layers Firstsource owns and operates, rather than inside the foundational models we rent.

Firstsource has multiple Agentic AI deployments operating in production or pilot for healthcare payor clients today, spanning claims triage, customer service orchestration, prior authorization, decision intelligence on claims and appeals, care management and payment integrity, and appeals and grievances workflows. Firstsource has multiple Agentic AI deployments operating in production or pilot for healthcare payor clients today, spanning claims triage, customer service orchestration, prior authorization, decision intelligence on claims and appeals, care management and payment integrity, and appeals and grievances workflows. All deployments share a common architectural foundation, integration surface, and governance model, which we describe below before turning to each deployment in turn.
Every agentic deployment operates on Kairos, Firstsource's operating system for AI-native operations. Kairos provides the runtime, the orchestration fabric, the governance scaffolding, and the audit trail that allow autonomous agents to operate safely and at scale within regulated payor environments.
At the center of Kairos sits the Intelligent Context Framework (ICF), Firstsource's proprietary context layer that gives our agents the domain-specific intelligence to reason and act in healthcare payor environments. Where most agentic systems today rely on generic LLM reasoning loosely connected to enterprise data, ICF supplies our agents with the contextual intelligence they need at runtime: payer policies and configurations, clinical guidelines, regulatory and compliance requirements (CMS, state, NCQA, URAC, HIPAA), claim attribute patterns, member life-event signals, provider network attributes, and the operational history of each client engagement. ICF is how Firstsource operationalizes Domain Intelligence — the first of the five tenets that anchor our Intelligence that Operates promise — and is the principal reason our agentic deployments perform reliably in production, rather than failing in the gaps between LLM reasoning and operational reality.
Within Kairos, our AI capabilities are organised as a portfolio of deep-domain technology assets and accelerators — pre-built platforms, frameworks, models, and solution accelerators built specifically for HealthTech, FinTech, and CXTech contexts. This portfolio gives our delivery teams a coherent set of reusable components, over one hundred proprietary copilots, decision agents, knowledge graphs, and accelerators, to compose into client-specific solutions, rather than building each engagement from first principles.

Our agents do not operate in isolation. They integrate natively with the client's existing payor estate — core administrative platforms (Facets, QNXT, Proclaim, PowerMHS, HealthRules Payer), CRM systems (Salesforce, AWS Connect), payment integrity tools (UiPath, Zelis, MPX, ClaimShark, Codoxo, Autonomize.AI), document and intake systems (Sympraxis, OCR/ICR pipelines), and BPaaS partner platforms (HealthEdge, mPulse, Edifecs, Reveleer). Agents read from and write to these systems through secure, governed APIs, ensuring that every action is traceable back to the calling agent and the underlying decision logic.
How we govern autonomy
Agentic AI introduces operational risk that copilots and traditional automation do not. Firstsource addresses this risk through three reinforcing layers of governance.
Principle-based governance. Every deployment is evaluated against eight standards — fairness, AI for good, regulatory compliance, accountability, interpretability, privacy and security, inclusiveness, and reliability. These principles translate into concrete acceptance criteria during model validation and into ongoing monitoring once a workflow is deployed.
Autonomy calibration through Progressive Trust. We do not deploy agents at full autonomy from day one. Every workflow begins under Human-in-the-Loop review at every decision, where the agent's output is approved or corrected before any downstream action is taken. As we accumulate evidence of sustained accuracy on a defined task, we graduate the workflow to Human-on-the-Loop, where the human supervises the agent's actions rather than approving each one. Only low-risk, high-confidence task domains progress to Human-above-the-Loop autonomy, and continuous post-hoc audit is maintained even at that level. This progression keeps our risk posture conservative and allows us to demonstrate compliance to regulators and clients alike.
Platform-level technical control. Lyzr provides reflection-based validation, groundedness checks against enterprise knowledge sources, fairness and bias safeguards, toxicity monitoring, automated PII detection and redaction, and token-level audit logs. Opus enforces compliance tracking and embeds explicit human review checkpoints at every workflow step.
Underlying all of this, our infrastructure is certified to ISO 27001, HITRUST, SOC 2 Type 2, and HIPAA. Business Associate Agreements cover every client engagement. A 24/7 Security Operations Center, operated in partnership with PwC on Microsoft Sentinel SIEM, monitors continuously across our environment.
Sympraxis as the intake and case-orchestration backbone
Several of the agentic deployments described below are integrated with Sympraxis® Health Plan Communication Hub — Firstsource intake and case-orchestration platform, deployed for 15 payor clients. Sympraxis ingests provider and member documents from multiple intake channels (mail, fax, portals, EDI), automates document classification, data extraction, summarization, and case creation through GenAI and OCR/ICR pipelines, and routes work into downstream queues. While Sympraxis itself is intelligent document processing rather than fully autonomous agentic execution, it provides the agentic triage and routing layer on which our downstream autonomous agents operate.

Responsible AI capabilities
Compliance with CMS and HIPAA for AI-driven decisions
For AI-driven decisions in payor environments, regulatory compliance is enforced at three layers: technical control, process control, and human authority.
At the technical layer, our infrastructure is certified to HIPAA, HITRUST CSF, SOC 2 Type 2, and ISO 27001, with Business Associate Agreements covering every payor client engagement. Encryption, access controls, audit logging, and breach notification capabilities meet or exceed HIPAA Security Rule requirements. For AI-specific governance, our control environment is aligned to ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management systems) and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.
At the process layer, we map each AI deployment to applicable federal and state regulations during use-case design. For prior authorization deployments specifically, our agents are designed to comply with the CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final Rule (CMS-0057-F), including the timeliness mandates that took effect in January 2026. For deployments touching Medicare Advantage coverage decisions, our agents are configured in line with CMS guidance that algorithms and AI models cannot be the sole basis for a coverage or medical necessity determination clinical reviewers retain authority, and AI outputs serve as decision support, not decision-making. Section 1557 non-discrimination requirements are reflected in our fairness testing protocols, and 21st Century Cures Act information-blocking obligations are addressed in our data access patterns.
At the human authority layer, every AI-driven decision that affects a member or provider coverage, payment, authorization, or appeals outcome — is either reviewed by a qualified human or governed by a Progressive Trust autonomy level that has been explicitly authorized by the client. Clinical decisions remain the responsibility of credentialed clinicians; payment decisions remain the responsibility of qualified claims professionals. AI accelerates and informs these decisions; it does not replace the regulated decision-maker.
Firstsource treats Responsible AI not as a policy document, but as an operating model. Every agentic and generative AI deployment in our payor portfolio operates under the same eight-principle Kairos Responsible AI framework, the same Progressive Trust calibration, the same platform-level controls, and the same multi-tier governance ownership. Regulatory compliance with CMS, HIPAA, Section 1557, and state-level requirements are enforced through technical certification, process design, and human authority working together. As regulatory expectations around AI in healthcare continue to evolve, including the CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final Rule and emerging state-level AI accountability legislation, our governance framework is designed to absorb new requirements without disrupting client operations.

What is your AI governance framework for payor clients — including model validation, drift monitoring, audit trails, and rollback mechanisms? (Describe the governance components in place — such as model validation, drift monitoring, audit trails, rollback mechanisms, and governance boards — including the frequency of each activity, who approves models before deployment, how incidents are escalated, and what the rollback SLA is.)
Our AI governance framework for payor clients is designed to make Intelligence that Operates safe, auditable, and production-ready. Kairos acts as the governance operating layer as much as the orchestration layer: it enforces deployment gates, captures traceability, calibrates autonomy through Progressive Trust, and supports rollback when performance or policy conditions require it.
Core governance components
Model validation: design review, data-lineage review, offline validation, fairness and error analysis, and workflow acceptance testing before pilot or production.
Autonomy calibration: workflows begin under Human-in-the-Loop oversight and graduate only after sustained performance and explicit sign-off.
Drift monitoring: production monitoring covers accuracy, confidence, throughput, exceptions, fairness signals, and input-distribution drift.
Audit trails: model version, workflow version, data access, decision path, overrides, and downstream actions are recorded and searchable.
Rollback and incident response: material failures trigger containment, root-cause analysis, rollback to a known-good version or manual fallback, client notification, and documented remediation.
Validation occurs before every material release. Monitoring is typically weekly during stabilization and monthly or quarterly in steady state, depending on risk. Rollback SLAs are defined by use case; for higher-risk workflows, fallback to a prior model or manual mode is typically targeted within hours, not days.
How do you manage data privacy and security when training or fine-tuning AI models on payor member/claims data? (Describe the data privacy controls in place — such as de-identification, synthetic data generation, federated learning, or HIPAA BAAs — including where payor data is stored during training, who has access, how consent and authorization are managed, and any certifications or third-party audits that validate your data privacy posture.)
When training or fine-tuning AI on payor member or claims data, we apply a privacy-by-design model. The starting principle is to use the least sensitive data required, prefer retrieval-grounded or configuration-driven approaches where possible, and where training is required, apply de-identification, access control, contractual controls, and auditable operating procedures throughout the lifecycle. This is managed through Kairos so that data handling, model promotion, and runtime usage remain governed under one operating model.
Core controls
De-identification: Safe Harbor or Expert Determination methods where appropriate; for many GenAI workflows we prefer RAG over broad fine-tuning on raw PHI.
Data minimization: only the minimum fields needed for the task are used; retention is defined by client contract and governance policy.
Logical segregation and access control: client data is segregated by client and environment; access is least-privilege, role-based, logged, and reviewed.
Secure storage and transfer: encryption in transit and at rest, governed environments, and auditable access pathways.
Contractual controls: BAAs, client-approved processing terms, audit rights, and incident-response obligations.
Training and tuning datasets are stored in client-approved cloud or enterprise environments aligned to regulatory and residency requirements. Access is restricted to authorized delivery, engineering, data science, and governance personnel on a documented need-to-know basis, and all access is auditable.

We maintain governance processes designed for the possibility of model failure, performance degradation, or bias drift in payor environments. As a matter of confidentiality, we do not disclose client-specific incidents publicly; however, where a material issue is detected, our response is consistent: contain the issue, reduce autonomy or revert to manual fallback, investigate root cause, remediate, disclose to the client as required, and only then restore normal operation. This response is built into Kairos and reinforced through Progressive Trust governance.
Standard response pattern
Detection: alerts, override patterns, QA sampling, fairness checks, client feedback, or exception spikes.
Containment: move to Human-in-the-Loop or manual fallback.
Root-cause analysis: determine whether the issue arose from data drift, policy change, prompt or retrieval error, model degradation, or workflow integration error.
Remediation: recalibration, data refresh, policy update, routing change, model rollback, or additional human review gates.
Disclosure and learning: notify the client per governance terms and feed the lessons back into validation thresholds, monitoring, and deployment standards.

Our approach to change management and AI adoption for payor workforces is based on a simple principle: AI succeeds only when people understand it, trust it, and see how their role improves with it. For that reason, change management is embedded into how we design, deploy, and scale every Kairos-enabled workflow; it is not a downstream communications activity.
What we do in practice
AI literacy and role-based education: frontline staff, supervisors, clinicians, QA teams, and business owners receive practical training on what the AI does, what it does not do, where human judgment remains essential, and how exceptions are handled.
Workflow redesign: we redesign handoffs, decision points, escalation paths, and supervisor roles so that humans and AI operate as one accountable system.
Upskilling for hybrid work: training shifts staff toward exception handling, judgment-intensive work, policy interpretation, monitoring, and coaching.
Champion networks: early adopters, team leads, and SMEs help build peer trust during pilot and early production.
Supervisor and governance enablement: managers are trained to interpret adoption dashboards, overrides, exceptions, and team-level performance under the new workflow.

input: If unresolved clinical appeals hit ~$5M/mo, how might AI denials tools change turnaround?
expected_output: If unresolved clinical appeals rose to about $5M/month, the same AI-enabled denials approach would likely materially shorten turnaround by automating triage, prioritizing high-value claims, and speeding appeal preparation. In the case study, clinical denial turnaround was reduced from 14 days to 3 days, with a 66% productivity improvement, 80% less manual triage, and a 65% reduction in medical necessity appeal handling time. Real-time analytics and scoring also helped focus teams on high-dollar and near-filing-limit claims faster.
context:
The Forrester Wave: Services Wave Case Study Submission
Please complete five case studies in the following slides, following the format provided. Please do not modify the slide templates. Refer to the questionnaire for specific criteria case studies should address.

Client overview and business need:
One of the largest health systems in the United States: NPR >$29.2B, >19,000 beds across 21 states.
Selected: as a trusted partner after the incumbent vendor gave insufficient insight into denial root causes; engagement began with clinical appeals.
Challenge: manual denials triage delayed resolution; limited real-time visibility into denial patterns and root causes; inconsistent appeal quality; documentation gaps and payer-policy complexity; ~$2.5M/month unresolved clinical appeals.
Roles impacted: revenue cycle leadership, denials and clinical appeals teams, clinical SMEs and in-house nurses, treating physicians.
Technologies: AI denials triage and scoring, GenAI appeal generation, payer-policy copilot, real-time analytics.
Firstsource: Client 1 – One of the largest US health systems (NPR >$29.2B)
Solution:
AI-enabled denials solution introduced within the client’s existing operations, targeting triage, prioritisation, appeal drafting and policy research.
Real-time analytics monitor denial root causes and trends; auto-triage routes key denial categories to the right teams.
Denials prioritised by recovery potential using propensity-to-deny/overturn scoring.
AI components: GenAI appeal generation aligned to payer policy; Medical Necessity and DRG AI analysis; Policy Advisor Copilot for instant payer-policy access.
Human-in-the-loop: clinical SMEs and nurses review complex cases and appeal strategy; physicians educated on payer-specific ED downgrade requirements.
Backlog reduced by focusing on high-dollar and near-filing-limit claims, with bi-weekly progress monitoring and real-time dashboards.
Other providers: introduced alongside the client’s incumbent denials vendor; Firstsource supplied clinical SMEs and nurses to review complex cases.

Are there examples from enterprise deployments on data foundation and setting up of context layer for AI/agentic layer? |  | 1444 | Context is the layer most AI programs skip. In Kairos it is an explicit product: the Intelligent Context Framework (ICF). ICF holds five registries - session context, entity context, immutable decision traces, execution signals and domain benchmarks - and performs three functions: capturing the reasoning and approvals core systems never record, converting tribal knowledge and manual overrides into searchable memory, and giving human and AI agents the context to handle exceptions well. ICF solves the problem of lost context across four key vectors - regulatory risk, revenue/margin leakage, talent drain and cycle of reinvention. ICF is a living, time-aware map linking business entities with decision traces, capturing the WHAT, WHY, WHO, and HOW behind every action. 

Readiness starts from execution truth, not documentation: sensors mine process, task, conversation, knowledge and document signals to establish how work actually happens. A knowledge engine then turns static SOPs into living operational knowledge, ingesting policies, transcripts, transactions, tickets and SME walkthroughs, extracting issue-to-resolution paths, capturing exceptions, surfacing undocumented workarounds and flagging SOP gaps.

For a MVNO, ICF helped with post-transition production shock. It captured edge cases & exceptions in KM, and compounded intelligence – for human and AI Agents. Impact : reduced AHT, Improved FTR and 30% reduced failure rate.
11103 | AI-Infused Customer Experience Operations | What kind of AI-enabled CX services, including agent assist, conversational AI, personalization, and automation exist? Are there adoption metrics and demonstrated customer outcomes? | Please provide one case study for this criterion in the Case Studies Template. | 1491 | CX is delivered as AI-first journeys, not AI added to a contact center. Agents run the decisions that matter, with guardrails, sensors, domain context and human oversight architected across the AI and learning loops.

In production: bilingual AI voice agents handling intake, triage and resolution inbound and outbound; conversational AI and chat; agent assist and copilots surfacing domain-guided next-best action; speech and sentiment analytics catching exceptions in flight; automated quality review across 100% of transcripts, not a sample; email and ticket triage routed by complexity and domain; personalization and customer 360; real-time translation and accent neutralization; biometric authentication.

Provider: AI voice agents run the Medicaid screening journey for a large US non-profit — 79% increase in screening rates on connected calls, 98% average patient satisfaction, ~70% lower agent cost, ~35% less telephony usage. Patient billing assistants are live across 20+ client implementations, with >30% of billing questions self-resolved.

Payer: a dental health plan moved call answer rate from 86% to 99%, speed of answer from 478 seconds to 5-6, first-call resolution to 97% and CSAT from 3.5 to 4.7. A health plan cut inbound volume 50%, with 35% of member contacts fully automated end to end.

Financial services: a UK bank cut monthly complaints 90% by shifting from reactive escalation to preventive intervention.

Case study: AI voice agents in eligibility screening.
11104 | AI-Enhanced Back-Office Operations | What kind of AI solutions used in finance, HR, procurement, claims, or other back-office functions exist? Are there quantified business outcomes and supporting case studies for these areas? | Please provide one case study for this criterion in the Case Studies Template. | 1386 | Back-office work runs on Kairos: GenAI, agentic AI and document intelligence orchestrated over the Intelligent Context Framework and Domain Harness, so every action carries the business rules, compliance controls and HITL escalation of the process it sits in. 

Finance, procurement and collections: invoice and payment processing, reconciliations, disputes, travel and expense, compliance reviews, propensity-to-pay modeling.
Claims and healthcare: claims processing, prior authorization, provider data, appeals and grievances, revenue cycle, digital intake.
Mortgage and banking: document intake, underwriting support, compliance validation, servicing, KYC/AML.
HR and shared services: employee copilots and conversational Ask-HR, knowledge retrieval, case management, attrition analytics, exit workflow automation.
Document intelligence: extraction, classification and validation across claims, mortgage and correspondence.

Outcomes: 40%+ of manual claims edits automated; provider-data cycle time down 80%; 66% RCM productivity gain; 80%+ straight-through processing in healthcare intake; mortgage cycle times 67% lower across 150K+ loans; 300M+ claims and mortgage pages processed; 99.2% compliance accuracy in collections; ~50 FTEs released at a UK bank through AI-led redaction.

Case study: from manual investigation to autonomous decisioning, UK commercial banking operations.
11105 | Intelligent Automation Delivery | What kind of integration of automation, AI, workflows, analytics, and orchestration technologies exist? How are these capabilities delivered consistently across engagements? |  | 1500 | Firstsource delivers Intelligent Automation through Kairos OS, that combines automation, AI, analytics, workflow orchestration, and governance into a single operating model, unifying five layers: systems of record; Operations Intelligence sensors in prevention, detection & learning modes; the Intelligent Context Framework for data enrichment, knowledge management & RAG; Domain Intelligence via the Domain Harness of skills, playbooks, policies & guardrails; and AI-native operations spanning agentic workflows, conversational AI & autonomous decisioning. Every layer is governed by continuous learning & LLMOps/AgentOps monitoring.

Consistency comes from:
-Engagement model: Transform-Implement-Operate as one continuous motion, giving repeatable diagnostics, build & run methodology
-Solution playbooks: 25+ years of domain expertise codified in the Domain Harness as a skills library, guardrails & evaluation frameworks
-Reference architectures: standardized deployment patterns per vertical - BFS, healthcare, HR, collections, telecom, retail, & utilities
-Platforms & solutions: 12+ proprietary platforms and 100+ accelerators

Quality gates at each Transform, Implement & Operate stage enforce governance, bias detection & compliance. Intelligent Context Framework helps identify and close gaps in process understanding, knowledge management coverage, training gaps, and business/product gaps, at every phase of this full-stack engagement model. This helps us reduce risk and time to value.

What is the rough distribution of engagements across fixed price, T&M, gain sharing, outcome oriented? What kind of impact AI adoption is making on engagement pricing for the clients? | Please provide one case study for this criterion in the Case Studies Template. | 1497 | We price for results, not effort, and commit to a number only once the baseline is documented.

Defined: every engagement opens with a diagnostic that sets the baseline both parties are measured against, then contracts named KPIs with agreed measurement protocols — explicit numeric thresholds, not best-efforts language. In provider operations, days in A/R under 38 and a 96%+ clean claim rate.

Commercialized through three constructs: percentage of collections, contingency on contracted KPI thresholds, and base-plus-bonus above the baseline.

Distribution: firm-wide, over 50% of revenue is output- or outcome-based, rising with practice maturity. Gain-share and success-fee constructs dominate mature operations where we hold baseline history. T&M is confined to transition, redesign and capability-building, where scope is genuinely uncertain. Fixed price is reserved for diagnostics and advisory, not ongoing operations. The mix differs by practice because we repeat the discovery-to-baseline sequence in each vertical rather than assuming it from adjacent work.

Tracked and governed: a shared analytics command center with ICF traceability behind every number; daily scorecards, monthly reviews and quarterly board reviews under one P&L owner.

AI decouples price from headcount: we default to output and outcome units, keep capacity pricing only where volume is genuinely unpredictable, and underwrite 2-5% net revenue uplift and 20-35% lower cost to collect.

Case study: A/R recovery.
11108 | Engagement Size And Complexity Capabilities | What are largest and most complex AI-enabled BPO deals executed? What are the smallest (non-PoC) paid BPO services engagement executed? Is there evidence of more advanced AI/agentic service delivery? |  | 1492 | Largest and most complex. Provider: a full-suite engagement for a 25-hospital national system, consolidating 12 vendors to one — A/R days 48 to 36, cost to collect 5.8% to 3.2%, +$28M net revenue in year one; separately, a $347M aged A/R placement returning 22.1% gross recovery, $77M collected. Payer: AI propensity models, process-mining sensors and a digital process twin across claims inventory, delivering ~$25M in savings. A US EHR and RCM provider: ~300 FTEs rebadged in a three-month transition with zero disruption, scaling to 27 new end clients in 18 months. Financial services: an AI-led operating model for a UK pension and benefits administrator — 300+ member journeys streamlined into 9 AI-first workflows at 95%+ quality.

Smallest paid, non-PoC: fully outsourced prior authorization for a 100-bed rural critical-access hospital — auth denial rate 18% to 6.2%, DSO 65 to 41 days, cost to collect down 32%.

Most advanced: an AI-native voice collector for a global cards and payments leader, run live against both manual and digital collections control groups. It beat the best-performing control group on promise-to-pay by 6%, scored higher on voice-of-customer than either, and proved 4x less likely to generate a complaint than the manual group — with zero complaints filed since inception. Cost savings against manual operations are double-digit.

Across the provider portfolio, nine of ten generative and agentic RCM solutions run in production with 1,500+ digital workers.
11107 | Transition And Transformation Execution | What transition methodologies are AI-enabled such as onboarding, knowledge transfer, process migration, and transformation frameworks? Our AI-First Transition Operating System runs ten AI-enabled stages from contract intake to continuous operations, each with human-in-the-loop control. AI extracts SLAs, penalties and compliance rules from the contract; process mining and LLM-led SME interviews convert system logs, transcripts and ticket data into a context graph (ICF) that auto-generates SOPs and training content.
