Adaptive training converts skill-gap profiles into personalized paths (~80% universal, 20% individualized) delivered through AI simulation. Process migration runs facilities, IT, access and bot deployment as parallel streams from a Transition Cockpit control tower. Continuous learning feeds post-go-live data into a reusable knowledge repository.

Internal benchmarking shows contract-to-go-live compressing 23 to 11 weeks (~52%) and knowledge-transfer-to-go-live 17 to 7 weeks (~59%), with 20-50% time reduction quantified across all 25 transition steps. These are modeled benchmarks; every new deal now carries a signed AI Charter measured on time to market, speed to competence, hiring accuracy and margin impact.
 | STRATEGY |  |  |  | 
10849 | Vision | What is the vision for the offering? How well articulated and differentiated is the vision? How does this vision impact the direction of this and/or adjacent markets? |  | 1499 | Our vision: to be the operator enterprises hold accountable for AI-run business processes — not the advisor who designs them or the vendor supplying the models. We call this Intelligence that Operates, delivered through Kairos, our operating system for AI-native operations. While doing this, we will continue to use human talent and knowledge to deliver the real moments that matter.

Intelligence gets cheaper and better every quarter. Accountability does not; it does not scale with compute. As agentic capability commoditizes, the scarce asset is a partner answerable for what the AI does in production.

We will not underwrite a workflow before its baseline is measured; we cap the outcome fee at a defined share of measured value, so we cannot earn more than the client saves. Over 50% of revenue is already output- or outcome-based.

Signing that requires four things. Domain depth to price risk in operations whose edge cases we know (Domain Intelligence, 25 years in regulated work). Right to answer for work we run (Full-Stack Delivery: design, build and run under one contract). A measured failure rate (Compounding Intelligence). A system we can explain (Governed Autonomy, trust earned per skill). Outcome Accountability is the fifth because it makes the other four possible.

Market direction: as buyers shift risk onto providers, consulting, software and managed services converge on one accountable operator — and providers who cannot price on outcomes get repriced by those who can.
10850 | Innovation | What is the approach to innovation for maintaining or obtaining a leadership position in this market? How does this approach anticipate and exhibit a commitment to innovation relevant to customer needs? What is the innovation strategy, including R&D budget? How well positioned is the strategy to execute on innovation given the history of innovation investments? |  | 1507 | Our innovation is powered by frontline intelligence, not just frontier intelligence, so it cannot be isolated into a single technology budget line. We are re-imagining all our internal and external facing enterprise workflows with an AI-1st lense, powered by Kairos.

The asset we compound is the Domain Harness: 25 years of operational judgment codified as executable skills, playbooks, guardrails and tests. The people encoding it are the examiners, coders, underwriters, nurses and advisors running the work.

In the loop, an expert corrects an agent's recommendation. On the loop, a specialist overrides an autonomous action; the override is traced to cause and the guardrail rewritten. Above the loop, an operations engineer reviews should-versus-did gaps — playbook against reality — and closes what neither human nor agent caught. Each pass promotes resolved failure into a versioned evaluation set and updates the governing policy, so the next execution is better.

Dedicated investment sits alongside it: 25+ technology centers of excellence, an AI innovation lab, 2,000+ AI-certified professionals, three platform launches and four acquisitions since 2024. Client advisory forums and co-innovation with hyperscaler and vertical partners set what we build next.

History shows it compounds. FY26 revenue grew ~20% on ~4.5% headcount growth, and HFS Research names Firstsource one of six providers worldwide sustaining non-linear growth through services as software across four consecutive quarters.
10851 | Partner ecosystem | What is the approach to developing and maintaining partnerships relevant to this market? What alliances/awards does the vendor have? How does the vendor leverage partnerships to drive differentiated work in this market? |  | 1488 | Approach: we position Kairos with partners, never on them. Kairos is agnostic to hyperscalers and frontier labs, and ~80% of its IP is vendor-neutral, so the same domain harness powers our agents, a client's agent platform, or a partner's stack without a rebuild. Clients get portability, composability and sovereignty, and add our layer rather than switching — making us additive to a partner's installed base.

Maintaining: partners are a managed portfolio, not a logo list, each classified on how they help us reimagine industry workflows and underwrite outcomes for intelligent operations. 

Alliances: 50+ partners across hyperscalers (AWS, Microsoft, Google), enterprise platforms (SFDC, ServiceNow, Zendesk), AI / automation specialists (Cresta, Parloa, UiPath, Celonis) and vertical AI specialists. We have several co-sell, marketplace and sell-through paths to market; equity in Lyzr.ai and Applied AI.

Recognition: Consistently recognized by industry analysts such as Everest, HfS, ISG, Avasant, NelsonHall, and several others for tech led leadership and non-linear business growth and profutability. 

Differentiated work: we do not compete with hyperscalers or AI control-tower platforms on governance infrastructure — we complete them. They govern which AI systems exist and what they may access; we generate the quality, attribution and context evidence that makes governance mean anything. Without an operator producing the evidence, a control tower governs an empty room.
10852 | Pricing flexibility and transparency | What pricing models are available to customers, and how easy are they to understand and adapt? |  | 1498 | Clients choose the meter; we hold the accountability. We price for results, not effort: firm-wide, over 50% of revenue is output- or outcome-based — per resolution, per unit processed or per dollar recovered — rising with practice maturity to ~90% in healthcare provider operations.

Four families are available, and clients blend them.
- Transaction and unit: per enrollment, per member, per chart coded, per page, per loan, per task.
- Outcome and success-linked: percentage of collections, contingency on recoveries, per successful enrollment.
- Workforce and capacity: per FTE, per agent, per call minute, where volume is unpredictable.
- Subscription and access: monthly platform fee, per admin user, account slabs, pay-as-you-go.

Easy to understand: each is one unit and one rate. Guarantees are explicit numeric thresholds, not best-efforts language. Where fees are outcome-linked, the percentage, value base and measurement criterion are disclosed at contracting, and a shared analytics command center lets the client verify performance live against the thresholds they pay on.

Easy to adapt: the pricing unit is decoupled from staffing. As AI absorbs volume, a contract moves from FTE to transaction to outcome without renegotiating the operating model: the work stays the same, only the meter changes. Entry is a fixed-fee diagnostic ending in a board-ready business case, scoped to the operation's complexity and data access — a baseline built on partial data cannot be priced against.
10855 | Talent strategy | How well does the talent strategy meet the needs of customers in terms of required skill sets, ability to maintain bench strength, and capacity to deliver quality experiences in engagements? How does it ensure consistent quality across different service lines/practices/regions? What investments does it make in talent programs? |  | 1462 | Firstsource's T-shaped talent strategy pairs shared horizontal capabilities (AI literacy, cognitive ability, data assimilation, empathy) with role-specific vertical expertise per service line.

Bench strength comes from a pre-certified college pipeline embedding the T-shaped framework into academic curricula—a steady, pre-skilled graduate supply instead of reactive hiring. The pipeline spans multiple cities and college networks, so bench depth isn't concentrated in one location and flexes with volume shifts.

Quality is protected upfront via AI-enabled, skill-first hiring: candidates are assessed against exact role capabilities before taking a call or case. A common horizontal foundation applies everywhere; vertical modules are customized per business line—so every team shares the same behavioral/AI baseline even as domain depth varies.

Assessments (cognitive suites, domain caselets, AI micro-tasks, simulations) are standardized and mapped to specific skills, keeping the hiring bar consistent across geography. Firstsource separates what it hires for (stable traits) from what it trains for (behaviors), so training closes gaps predictably.

Capacity: 36,000+ people, 12 countries. Consistency holds via versioned artifacts, not supervisory culture. Automated QA scores 100% of work, not a sample.

Investment: 160+ academy programs (10 countries), 200,000+ digital learning hours (FY25), 2,500+ internal moves, 2,000+ AI-certified professionals.
10856 | Global delivery strategy | How does the provider deliver global programs? How does the org structure support global client needs? How successful is the provider delivering services for global enterprises? |  | 1424 | Firstsource delivers global programs through pods—a repeatable unit combining automated and human agents. The mix is decided by work type, not location or cost: regulatory exposure, irreversible consequences, or a distressed customer always goes to a person. Everything else is routed to automation, supervised automation, or a person based on task definition, specialist knowledge, and context needed. Local regulations are handled by adjusting rules, not redesigning processes per market.

Each pod has six roles: pod leader (commercials, client relationship), orchestrator (routing, escalations), analyst (automation build), shared technical specialist (platform/integration), and the human/automated agents doing the work. Multi-country programs scale by adding pods under layered governance—local ownership, consolidated reporting. Non-proprietary learnings are stored centrally, so the operation improves continuously.

Leadership is organized by industry (healthcare, BFS, CMT, collections, CX), with a single P&L owner per engagement guaranteeing end-to-end performance.

Footprint: 36,000+ people, 57 centers, 12 countries. Onshore, nearshore, offshore capacity with follow-the-sun coverage; HIPAA, PCI-DSS, FCA, CFPB, SOC 2 compliance is standard.

Scale: 250+ clients (Fortune 500, FTSE 100), top-5 tenure 17+ years, FY26 revenue $1,082M, 17 large deals, 47 new logos, 9th straight quarter of double-digit growth.

context:
The Business Process Outsourcing Services Landscape, Q2 2026 
Forrester invites you to participate in our research to support the upcoming Forrester Landscape 
Business Process Outsourcing Services, Q2 2026 report by VP, Principal Analyst Ashutosh Sharma. 
We define Business Process Outsourcing Services as: 
 
Service providers that use artificial intelligence to manage and execute customer-facing and back-
office business processes on behalf of clients, including acquiring and managing human and digital 
talent; serving customers in existing and new digital channels; and using back-office services and 
specialized vertical, insight, and technology-led frameworks to optimize end-to-end customer journeys. 
(This definition is subject to change prior to publication.) 
Research Premise  
Landscape reports help our clients identify, understand, and explore the providers that align with 
clients’ critical business technology. The Landscape report will: 
• Define the Business Process Outsourcing Services marketplace, market maturity, and top market 
dynamics. 
• Present an overview of providers in the market, including geographic and industry focuses and 
top business scenarios. 
• Identify the top business scenarios for the Business Process Outsourcing Services and the 
capability required to address them.  
 
In July, we intend to kick off a Forrester Wave evaluation on this market. We may use information in 
the Landscape questionnaire to screen for participation in the subsequent Forrester Wave. 
Participation in this Landscape does not guarantee inclusion in the subsequent Forrester Wave. 
Research Timeline 
Research questionnaire due: April 7, 2026 
Approximate publication: June 2026 
Research Process 
We invite providers with a Business Process Outsourcing Services offering to complete a 
questionnaire to determine inclusion as a notable provider in the Landscape report. This questionnaire 
asks about:  
1. Your market position, defined in terms of regions, industries, and revenue. 
2. The most important business scenarios you help your clients address/focus on.  
3. An overview of your services and delivery platforms.  
4. Your view of market position and key market dynamics. 
If you choose not to participate or do not submit a fully completed questionnaire, we may still include 
your company in the report using Forrester estimates.

Overview of Business Scenarios in Landscapes 
Forrester’s Landscape reports help clients understand the top business scenarios in a market in 
addition to the providers. As part of this analysis, Forrester segments the business scenarios as core 
(the business scenarios virtually all providers in the market cover and the main business scenarios a 
buyer is looking to solve for) and extended (business scenarios some buyers look to address in 
addition to the core, but may be less frequently addressed by solutions in this space). To help 
Forrester clients learn where providers differ in focus beyond the core business scenarios, providers 
will be asked to select your top three extended business scenarios that you focus on within the survey, 
and these selections will be shown in a figure in the report. For this market, we have segmented the 
business scenarios as following: 
Core business scenarios: 
• AI-enhanced back office: Back-office services delivered with workflows that are optimized with 
AI powered automation and/or agents. 
• AI-infused customer experience: Services that leverage AI to deliver improved customer 
experience through capabilities such as personalization, data, and analytics in real time. 
• Intelligent automation: Services that automate back-office processes while embedding 
intelligence, e.g. through AI + RPA combination. 
 
Extended business scenarios: 
• AI consulting for business process support: Services that help clients redesign and reimagine 
their business processes using AI to maximize the value of outsourcing. 
• Analytics services: Data and analytics services that support context engineering and beyond, 
for both human and digital agents. 
• Industry AI services: Industry specific AI services through specialized training of AI models or 
other means. 
• AI governance: Services that deliver ethical, responsible, secure-by-design use of AI, fully 
compliant with all applicable regulations. 
Provider Graphics Preview 
Following Forrester’s analysis of the aggregate data, Forrester will send included providers the 
provider-focused graphics, which include information pulled directly from the questionnaire responses. 
This is a courtesy to show the representation of the self-reported data provided in the questionnaire 
related to revenue, industries, geographies, and specialty business scenarios. This is not an 
opportunity to revise answers submitted in the questionnaire. We will also share a Courtesy Preview of 
the full report prior to publication. 
The Forrester Research Team 
Analyst: Ashutosh Sharma, VP, Principal Analyst 
Project Manager: Laura Demarki, Associate Project Manager, ldemarki@forrester.com  
 
If you have any questions concerning this report or what we will need from you, please contact Laura. 
Thank you!
source_file: The Business Process Outsourcing Services Landscape, Q2 2026 - Report Premise.pdf

context:
Award categories
1. Best Services-as-Software Transformation
Enterprise–provider collaboration that reimagines service delivery using AI, automation, reusable IP, or agentic models — with measurable business results.
2. Best ‘Services Eating Software’
Service providers embedding proprietary software, AI, and automation into delivery to create scalable, intelligent operating models.
3. Best ‘Software Eating Services’
Software vendors replacing heavy customization and consulting with intelligent automation, embedded decisioning, and adaptive AI capabilities.
4. Best Startup / Emerging Firm
Next-generation firms built from inception around AI-native, outcome-centric, scalable models.
5. Best Services-as-Software Transformation by a GCC / GBS
Global Capability Centers evolving from cost centers into AI-enabled innovation engines driving enterprise-wide value.


## 1. Best Services-as-Software Transformation
Q1. Why This Matters – What Problem We Are Solving
Response: Enterprises are facing a seismic shift in how work, workforce, and workflows operate. 
The rise of gig talent, AI-led gig platforms, 
niche skill access, and 
remote-work normalization is reshaping workforce models.

expected_output:
The brochure’s provider eligibility criteria align closely with common agentic AI evaluation focus areas, but they are broader and more operational.

Key overlaps:
- Autonomy and orchestration: The brochure requires enterprise-grade agentic AI solutions, multi-agent orchestration, autonomous planning and adaptive workflows.
- Tool/API integration: It emphasizes secure tool use, API integration and execution boundaries.
- Memory and context: It includes long-context memory, RAG, knowledge graphs, and contextual memory frameworks.
- Human oversight and safety: It requires human-in-the-loop checkpoints, explainability, policy-based controls and real-time monitoring.
- Governance and compliance: It highlights bias mitigation, transparency, auditability, security and regulatory compliance.
- Operations and monitoring: It includes LLMOps/AgentOps, observability, prompt/version management and FinOps.

Additional brochure criteria beyond typical eval focus areas:
- Production readiness beyond PoCs
- Industry-specific accelerators and client case studies
- Partner ecosystem strength with hyperscalers, model providers and ISVs
- Ability to scale distributed execution in enterprise environments

So, agentic AI eval focus areas are generally reflected in the brochure, while the brochure adds stronger emphasis on enterprise deployment maturity, ecosystem breadth and business proof points.

The Big Story
Lumine Goes Live

LUMINE

Lumine, a new partner intelligence copilot built by our Global Partnerships team, went live in early beta on May 4. Designed as an always-on intelligence layer for the partnerships function, it helps teams quickly surface structured, actionable insights on partners and prospects, faster and with greater depth than traditional research methods allow.

In practice, Lumine helps turn scattered information into clearer, more usable intelligence for the people who need it most. For Sales and Solution leaders, that means sharper preparation, more consistent partner insight, and a controlled way to access information that was once harder and slower to pull together. It also gives teams more time to focus on conversations and relationships instead of manual research.

Lumine is a strong example of Brilliant People powered by Bold Tech. Rather than simply talking about AI, the team has built it into the workflow in a practical way that supports better decisions and stronger execution. As broader rollout continues, Lumine shows how AI can make intelligence more accessible, useful, and operational across Firstsource.

 | ISG Provider Lens® Research Methodology


Quadrant Methodology


ISG Provider Lens® quadrant evaluation framework is robust and adopts a systematic approach to arrive at the final scoring. Based on the scoring and relative positioning, the companies are identified as Leaders, Challengers, Contenders or Rising Stars. 


ISG Provider Lens® - Our Data Sources


ISG Provider Lens® research studies analyze relevant software vendors/service providers in a particular market, based on a multi-phased research and analysis process, and positions these providers based on the ISG research methodology. For both quadrant and archetype reports, the evaluation framework takes the following into consideration:


	    1. Primary research: Survey input from service providers/vendors

	    2. Secondary research: Desk research on publicly available data

	    3. Advisory input: Thoughts/inputs of ISG advisors

	    4. Star of Excellence*: Client feedback about the company on multiple parameters

	    5. ISG internal, proprietary databases such as deal information

	    6. Balance between qualitative and quantitative parameters




NOTE: The key parameters are highlighted as per the standard methodology. There will be variations in parameters, depending on the topic of evaluation. 5 | Please share and describe some of the prevalent obstacles that prevent PoCs from reaching the production stage. Additionally, elaborate on the strategies and solutions employed to surmount these challenges. |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
 | In enterprise environments, GenAI PoCs frequently fail to reach production due to data access constraints, integration complexity, fast‑changing GenAI stacks, unclear value realization, and lack of production‑grade governance. Kairos, Firstsource’s AI operating system for “Intelligence That Operates,” is explicitly designed to overcome these barriers by unifying strategy, execution, and governance into a single operating layer that supports reliable scale‑up from day one.

Key Obstacles and Strategies Employed
1.Limited access to production‑grade data in regulated domains: In Healthcare and BFSI, access to real production data is tightly controlled, with long approval cycles slowing PoC progress.
Strategy employed: Leveraging data governance and synthetic data frameworks, we generate production‑like synthetic datasets using domain expertise and AI models. This enables realistic testing and validation while remaining compliant with privacy and regulatory requirements.

2.Complexity of upstream and downstream system integration:PoCs often fail when workflows are incomplete across heterogeneous IT landscapes spanning legacy mainframes and modern API‑based systems.

Orchestration, task planning, and execution:
-Goal‑driven orchestration: Decomposes business goals into discrete tasks and sub‑tasks, assigns them to specialized agents, and coordinates execution through defined workflows rather than ad‑hoc agent calls.
-Deterministic + agentic execution: Each workflow combines deterministic steps (rules, validations) with agentic reasoning where ambiguity or decision‑making is required, ensuring predictable outcomes.
-Workflow automation: Orchestration spans CRM systems, ERP platforms, data pipelines, IoT feeds, and industry platforms, embedding agentic execution directly into existing operational flows.

Integration with external tools, APIs, and enterprise applications
-Controlled tool and API access: Agents interact with enterprise tools only through pre‑approved APIs and connectors, with scopes and permissions defined at design time.
-Multi‑system coordination: Supports orchestration across CRM, ERP,billing systems, ticketing platforms, and event streams, enabling end‑to‑end automation without disrupting legacy environments.
-Event‑ and API‑driven patterns: Supports synchronous and asynchronous execution, enabling agents to respond to real‑time events (for example, data updates or exceptions).

Multi‑agent collaboration and workflow automation
-Role‑based agents: Workflows are executed by multiple agents with clearly defined roles (for example, intake, validation, decisioning, execution, escalation).
-Explicit hand‑offs: Agent interactions follow predefined coordination logic, preventing uncontrolled agent‑to‑agent behavior.
-Human‑in‑the‑loop (HITL): Mandatory checkpoints are enforced for high‑risk, regulated, or judgment‑heavy steps.

State and memory strategy
-Scoped task memory: Agents maintain short‑lived, task‑specific context required for execution, avoiding uncontrolled long‑term memory.
-Workflow‑level state management: State transitions across tasks and agents to ensure resumability, consistency, and traceability.
-No cross‑client memory leakage: Memory is isolated per workflow and client environment.

Failure and exception handling
-Graceful degradation: If an agent or tool call fails, workflows fall back to predefined retry, alternate paths, or HITL escalation.
-Exception routing: Failures are categorized, logged, and routed to human operators or supervisory agents based on severity.
-Safe rollback: Partial executions can be paused or rolled back without corrupting enterprise systems.

Observability, tracing, and auditability
-End‑to‑end observability: captures tool/API call logs, agent action traces, decision rationales, and escalation events.
-Operational KPIs: 35+ metrics track performance, drift, latency, and compliance across workflows.
-Audit‑ready logs: All actions are time‑stamped, immutable, and traceable for regulatory and risk reviews.

Sandboxing and safe execution boundaries
-Sandboxed execution: Agents operate within isolated runtime environments with strict boundaries on tool access, data scope, and execution rights.
-Policy‑enforced guardrails: enforces permissioning, data access rules, and safety policies before any tool or API invocation.
-No free‑form execution: Agents cannot execute arbitrary code or actions outside approved workflows |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Quadrant Methodology


ISG Provider Lens® quadrant evaluation framework is robust and adopts a systematic approach to arrive at the final scoring. Based on the scoring and relative positioning, the companies are identified as Leaders, Challengers, Contenders or Rising Stars. 


ISG Provider Lens® - Our Data Sources


ISG Provider Lens® research studies analyze relevant software vendors/service providers in a particular market, based on a multi-phased research and analysis process, and positions these providers based on the ISG research methodology. For both quadrant and archetype reports, the evaluation framework takes the following into consideration:


	    1. Primary research: Survey input from service providers/vendors

	    2. Secondary research: Desk research on publicly available data

	    3. Advisory input: Thoughts/inputs of ISG advisors

	    4. Star of Excellence*: Client feedback about the company on multiple parameters

	    5. ISG internal, proprietary databases such as deal information

	    6. Balance between qualitative and quantitative parameters

-At the organizational context layer, GenAI solutions—including virtual assistants, forecasting copilots, QA automation, and AI‑driven coaching—leverage session context, entity context, decision traces, execution signals, and domain benchmarks to deliver context‑aware, explainable, and audit‑ready intelligence. Capabilities such as the Agentic AI Studio and the GenAI Task Execution Platform provide scalable task execution, built‑in governance, auditability, and human‑in‑the‑loop controls, with continuous feedback loops that compound intelligence over time.

Across all layers, responsible AI governance—covering security, privacy, ethics, explainability, and compliance—is embedded by design, ensuring enterprise trust, regulatory readiness, and sustainable GenAI adoption throughout the lifecycle.

Over the next 12–24 months, our vision is to evolve GenAI services from point solutions to enterprise-grade, agent-led transformation platforms. Key focus areas include:

-Scaling Agentic AI adoption to support autonomous, outcome-driven business processes.
-Expanding industry-specific GenAI solutions and accelerators to drive faster time-to-value.
-Strengthening AI governance, risk, and compliance capabilities as regulations and enterprise adoption mature.
-Deepening hyperscaler and ecosystem partnerships to support multi-model, hybrid, and secure enterprise deployments.
-Enabling clients to move from productivity-led GenAI use cases to revenue, experience, and decision-impact use cases. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

 | In enterprise environments, GenAI PoCs frequently fail to reach production due to data access constraints, integration complexity, fast‑changing GenAI stacks, unclear value realization, and lack of production‑grade governance. Kairos, Firstsource’s AI operating system for “Intelligence That Operates,” is explicitly designed to overcome these barriers by unifying strategy, execution, and governance into a single operating layer that supports reliable scale‑up from day one.

Key Obstacles and Strategies Employed
1.Limited access to production‑grade data in regulated domains: In Healthcare and BFSI, access to real production data is tightly controlled, with long approval cycles slowing PoC progress.
Strategy employed: Leveraging data governance and synthetic data frameworks, we generate production‑like synthetic datasets using domain expertise and AI models. This enables realistic testing and validation while remaining compliant with privacy and regulatory requirements.

2.Complexity of upstream and downstream system integration:PoCs often fail when workflows are incomplete across heterogeneous IT landscapes spanning legacy mainframes and modern API‑based systems.
Strategy employed: Using modular, microservices‑based architecture, we adopt a hybrid integration approach—combining API‑based integrations for modern platforms with RPA‑enabled connectors for legacy systems—to ensure end‑to‑end workflow completeness and operational autonomy.

3.Rapid technological shifts in GenAI platforms and models:The fast‑evolving GenAI ecosystem (new LLMs, agentic frameworks, orchestration tools, and pricing models) creates uncertainty and hesitation in committing PoCs to production architectures.
Strategy employed: Kairos is designed as a model‑ and platform‑agnostic framework, enabling abstraction across LLM providers, orchestration layers, and infrastructure. This protects client investments by allowing technology components to evolve without re‑architecting core workflows.

4.Business case validation and executive sign‑off delays:Technically successful PoCs may stall without a clearly quantified and outcome‑linked business case aligned to enterprise priorities.
Strategy employed: Through AI Labs and Innovation Studios, we define KPIs early, measure tangible value (productivity gains, cost‑to‑serve reduction, risk mitigation), and showcase results via executive demos and value dashboards, accelerating stakeholder alignment and approvals.

5.Governance, risk, and operational readiness gaps:Many PoCs are built without considering production‑grade requirements such as security, auditability, monitoring, and change management.
Strategy employed: We embed governance‑by‑design using Kairos frameworks, including Responsible AI controls, human‑in‑the‑loop mechanisms, audit trails, security guardrails, and operational monitoring, ensuring PoCs are production‑ready from inception.

6.Skills, adoption, and operating model readiness:Lack of AI‑ready skills and unclear ownership between business, IT, and risk teams can slow scale‑up.
Strategy employed: engagements include operating model design, change enablement, and targeted upskilling, ensuring clear accountability, adoption readiness, and sustained value realization post‑deployment. |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Orchestration, task planning, and execution:
-Goal‑driven orchestration: Decomposes business goals into discrete tasks and sub‑tasks, assigns them to specialized agents, and coordinates execution through defined workflows rather than ad‑hoc agent calls.
-Deterministic + agentic execution: Each workflow combines deterministic steps (rules, validations) with agentic reasoning where ambiguity or decision‑making is required, ensuring predictable outcomes.
-Workflow automation: Orchestration spans CRM systems, ERP platforms, data pipelines, IoT feeds, and industry platforms, embedding agentic execution directly into existing operational flows.

Integration with external tools, APIs, and enterprise applications
-Controlled tool and API access: Agents interact with enterprise tools only through pre‑approved APIs and connectors, with scopes and permissions defined at design time.
-Multi‑system coordination: Supports orchestration across CRM, ERP,billing systems, ticketing platforms, and event streams, enabling end‑to‑end automation without disrupting legacy environments.
-Event‑ and API‑driven patterns: Supports synchronous and asynchronous execution, enabling agents to respond to real‑time events (for example, data updates or exceptions).

Multi‑agent collaboration and workflow automation
-Role‑based agents: Workflows are executed by multiple agents with clearly defined roles (for example, intake, validation, decisioning, execution, escalation).
-Explicit hand‑offs: Agent interactions follow predefined coordination logic, preventing uncontrolled agent‑to‑agent behavior.
-Human‑in‑the‑loop (HITL): Mandatory checkpoints are enforced for high‑risk, regulated, or judgment‑heavy steps.

State and memory strategy
-Scoped task memory: Agents maintain short‑lived, task‑specific context required for execution, avoiding uncontrolled long‑term memory.
-Workflow‑level state management: State transitions across tasks and agents to ensure resumability, consistency, and traceability.
-No cross‑client memory leakage: Memory is isolated per workflow and client environment.

Failure and exception handling
-Graceful degradation: If an agent or tool call fails, workflows fall back to predefined retry, alternate paths, or HITL escalation.
-Exception routing: Failures are categorized, logged, and routed to human operators or supervisory agents based on severity.
-Safe rollback: Partial executions can be paused or rolled back without corrupting enterprise systems.

Observability, tracing, and auditability
-End‑to‑end observability: captures tool/API call logs, agent action traces, decision rationales, and escalation events.
-Operational KPIs: 35+ metrics track performance, drift, latency, and compliance across workflows.
-Audit‑ready logs: All actions are time‑stamped, immutable, and traceable for regulatory and risk reviews.

Sandboxing and safe execution boundaries
-Sandboxed execution: Agents operate within isolated runtime environments with strict boundaries on tool access, data scope, and execution rights.
-Policy‑enforced guardrails: enforces permissioning, data access rules, and safety policies before any tool or API invocation.
-No free‑form execution: Agents cannot execute arbitrary code or actions outside approved workflows |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

13 | How do you align commercial structures with performance-based outcomes while mitigating enterprise risks? |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
 | Firstsource aligns commercial structures with performance‑based outcomes through a governed, risk‑aware contracting and delivery model, anchored on Kairos Agentic AI Suite, ensuring value realization without exposing enterprises to uncontrolled operational or compliance risk.

Aligning commercials to outcomes
-Outcome‑linked pricing constructs: Commercials are tied to clearly defined business KPIs (for example cycle‑time reduction, cost‑to‑serve improvement, quality uplift, or automation coverage), rather than raw consumption or effort alone.
-Milestone‑based value realization: Contracts are structured with phased milestones (pilot → scale → optimize), allowing outcome measurement before expanding scope or autonomy.
-Shared value models: Where appropriate, gain‑share or productivity‑linked pricing is applied, ensuring incentives are aligned between Firstsource and the client.

Risk mitigation mechanisms
-Phased autonomy and scope control: Agentic AI deployments begin with assistive or supervised modes and progress to higher autonomy only after KPI stability, governance readiness, and risk acceptance are demonstrated.
-Baseline protection clauses: Contracts include baseline definitions, caps, and floors to prevent volatility from external factors (volume spikes, regulatory change, data quality issues).
-Human‑in‑the‑loop safeguards: High‑risk, regulated, or judgment‑heavy activities retain mandatory HITL checkpoints, limiting downside risk while still enabling performance gains.

Governance and assurance
-Transparent measurement and auditability: Monitor provides continuous visibility into performance metrics, agent behavior, and outcome attribution, enabling objective validation of results.
-Runbooks and exception handling: Operational runbooks define fallback paths, escalation, rollback, and remediation procedures to protect business continuity.
-Compliance‑by‑design: Data protection, audit trails, and policy enforcement are embedded contractually and technically, reducing regulatory and operational exposure. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

 | Yes, Firstsource has developed purpose‑built reference architectures, operating frameworks, and governance models specifically for enterprise‑grade agentic AI, operationalized through Kairos Agentic AI Suite.

Firstsource has defined a modular, enterprise‑grade agentic AI reference architecture that standardizes how agents are designed, orchestrated, governed, and scaled. Key elements include:
-Multi‑agent orchestration layer for goal‑driven task decomposition and coordination
-Clear separation of deterministic, generative, and agentic layers to ensure predictability
-API‑first integration architecture to embed agents into CRM, ERP, ITSM, data platforms, and industry systems
-Isolated runtime and memory scopes for agent safety and data protection
This architecture is implemented via the Agentic AI Studio (Xplore, Evaluate, Weave, Monitor).

2. Agentic AI Lifecycle & Operating Framework
Firstsource has built an end‑to‑end agentic AI lifecycle framework, covering:
-Discover: Agentic AI readiness and use‑case fitment assessment across 11 dimensions
-Design: Definition of agent roles, autonomy boundaries, escalation paths, and KPIs
-Deploy: Controlled rollout using canary releases, HITL checkpoints, and audit controls
-Operate: AgentOps model with continuous monitoring, drift detection, and performance optimization
-Evolve: Learning loops, regression testing, and controlled expansion of autonomy
This framework ensures agentic AI moves from pilot to production safely and repeatably.

3. Governance‑First Agentic AI Model
Firstsource has developed a governance‑by‑design model for agentic AI, embedded into Kairos, which includes:
-Explicit autonomy tiers (advisory, supervised agentic, controlled autonomy)
-Human‑in‑the‑loop (HITL) enforcement for regulated or judgment‑heavy workflows
-Policy‑aware agent behavior, including regulatory rules, SOPs, and enterprise constraints
-End‑to‑end auditability, with decision traces, tool/API logs, and escalation records
This governance model is applied consistently across industries, especially BFSI, Healthcare, and Utilities.

-Mortgage Language Model (MLM) as a domain‑constrained, policy‑aware reasoning layer for underwriting
-SOP‑driven agentic workflows for claims, KYC screening, service desk, and utilities operations

input: If Kairos entered a new client ops, how would its 5-layer AI-native OS work?
expected_output:
Kairos would work as a 5-layer stack that turns client operations into AI-native operations:

1. **Raw Data & Transactions**: Connects to systems of record like CRM, billing, field service, collections, and channels.  
2. **Operations Intelligence**: Uses **Sensors** such as process mining, task mining, conversation intelligence, knowledge mining, and document intelligence to detect how work actually happens.  
3. **Organisational Context**: Builds memory through the **Intelligent Context Framework (ICF)** using session context, entity context, decision traces, execution signals, and domain benchmarks.  
4. **Domain Intelligence**: Applies the **Domain Harness** with skills libraries, playbooks, policies, guardrails, authoring, and evaluation—encoding 25 years of expertise as executable intelligence.  
5. **AI-Native Operations**: Deploys agents for tasks like discovery, acquisition, triage, scheduling, payments, and complaints.

The system then runs in a **continuous learning loop**, so every decision and engagement makes the operating system smarter.

input: Outline ISG Intelligent Automation Services 2026 RFI structure, incl. IVCA, AIOps, delivery centers, case studies.
expected_output:
The ISG Intelligent Automation Services 2026 RFI is structured as follows:

1. General / Company Overview  
- Company name, quadrant/region participation, 3-year strategy, 12–18 month GTM strategy  
- Investment plans, training/reskilling, revenue/clients/FTEs, geographic and industry splits  
- Partner ecosystem, awards, certifications, GenAI/agentic AI stage, innovation, ESG, responsible AI

2. Industry Value Chain Automation (IVCA)  
- Focuses on proprietary, industry-specific intelligent automation solutions  
- Covers USP, proprietary platforms/solutions, associated services, revenue/clients/FTEs, pricing models  
- Includes frameworks/IP, deployment/hosting, process automation metrics, GenAI/agentic AI use cases, security, trends, differentiators and competitors

3. AI for IT Operations (AIOps)  
- Focuses on proprietary AIOps platforms for monitoring, observability, event intelligence and remediation  
- Covers offering description, service scope, revenue/clients/FTEs, pricing, compliance/security, frameworks/IP  
- Includes process complexity, supported functions, AI/ML and GenAI/agentic AI capabilities, integrations, use cases, trends, differentiators and competitors

4. Delivery Centers / GCC worksheet  
- Requires overall number of delivery centers  
- Detailed center-by-center data: country, year established, city, center type, FTEs, YoY FTE growth, services offered, skills and comments

5. Case Studies  
- Submitted separately through: https://surveys.isg-one.com/survey/selfserve/48f8/251211  
- Used for IPL evaluation, Case Study Standouts, Paragon Awards and CPQ inputs  
- Assessed on six pillars including client context, innovation, execution, outcomes and sustainability/change enablement

6. Star of Excellence client nominations  
- Submitted separately through: https://surveys.isg-one.com/survey/selfserve/48f8/241022  
- Used for confidential client feedback across IPL, CX Star Performer, Star of Excellence Awards and CPQ

Additional scope notes:
- Quadrants covered: IVCA and AIOps
- Geographic coverage: U.S. and Europe
- Final submission deadline: July 17, 2026
- Financial data must be recorded in U.S. dollars

 | ISG Provider Lens® Research Methodology


Quadrant Methodology


ISG Provider Lens® quadrant evaluation framework is robust and adopts a systematic approach to arrive at the final scoring. Based on the scoring and relative positioning, the companies are identified as Leaders, Challengers, Contenders or Rising Stars. 


ISG Provider Lens® - Our Data Sources


ISG Provider Lens® research studies analyze relevant software vendors/service providers in a particular market, based on a multi-phased research and analysis process, and positions these providers based on the ISG research methodology. For both quadrant and archetype reports, the evaluation framework takes the following into consideration:


	    1. Primary research: Survey input from service providers/vendors

	    2. Secondary research: Desk research on publicly available data

	    3. Advisory input: Thoughts/inputs of ISG advisors

	    4. Star of Excellence*: Client feedback about the company on multiple parameters

	    5. ISG internal, proprietary databases such as deal information

	    6. Balance between qualitative and quantitative parameters

 | ISG Provider Lens® Research Methodology


Quadrant Methodology


ISG Provider Lens® quadrant evaluation framework is robust and adopts a systematic approach to arrive at the final scoring. Based on the scoring and relative positioning, the companies are identified as Leaders, Challengers, Contenders or Rising Stars. 


ISG Provider Lens® - Our Data Sources


ISG Provider Lens® research studies analyze relevant software vendors/service providers in a particular market, based on a multi-phased research and analysis process, and positions these providers based on the ISG research methodology. For both quadrant and archetype reports, the evaluation framework takes the following into consideration:


	    1. Primary research: Survey input from service providers/vendors

	    2. Secondary research: Desk research on publicly available data

	    3. Advisory input: Thoughts/inputs of ISG advisors

	    4. Star of Excellence*: Client feedback about the company on multiple parameters

	    5. ISG internal, proprietary databases such as deal information

	    6. Balance between qualitative and quantitative parameters




NOTE: The key parameters are highlighted as per the standard methodology. There will be variations in parameters, depending on the topic of evaluation. input: Summarize FSL’s UnBPO→Kairos vision, incl. AI-native utility, M2C lifecycle, and sustainability.
expected_output:
FSL’s UnBPO→Kairos vision is to create an AI-native utility operating model that moves beyond traditional BPO to “intelligence that operates.” It combines Kairos OS + UnBPO to unify AI, automation, analytics, and utility domain consulting across the full meter-to-cash lifecycle—acquire, fulfill, serve, and retain.

Key elements include:
- AI-native operations: predictive billing, auto exception handling, agentic workflows, autonomous decisioning, digital twins, remote triage, and digital field force.
- End-to-end M2C coverage: smart metering, M2C, customer experience, collections, and field services in a connected, hyper-automated model.
- Customer-centric CX: omnichannel journeys, AI agents/bots/voice AI, proactive self-service, personalization, and vulnerability detection.
- Digital core modernization: integration with SAP, Oracle, Salesforce, CIS, MDMS, cloud platforms, plus CRM and CCaaS.
- Data intelligence: real-time dashboards, forecasting, revenue leakage detection, and AI-led insights such as churn, propensity to pay, and CLTV.
- Sustainability and resilience: support for DERs, EVs, smart grids, prosumer models, water reuse, and NRW, with built-in ESG and regulatory guardrails.

Overall, the goal is resilient, customer-centric, efficient, and sustainable utilities delivered at global scale.

input: If cust. PII is pasted into a chatbot, what policy violations and approved processing apply?
expected_output:
Pasting customer PII into a chatbot is a policy violation unless the tool is explicitly certified for Sensitive data.

Relevant violations:
- Sensitive data must never be pasted into web-based chat interfaces of productivity tools.
- Inputting Sensitive Data into Chatbots is prohibited for conversational AI interfaces, even enterprise versions, unless explicitly certified for that data level.
- If the chatbot is unapproved, personal, or free-tier, it is also a Shadow AI violation.

Approved processing for customer PII:
- Only use restricted/private cloud AI platforms hosted on major CSPs.
- Processing must occur via secure APIs within product infrastructure, not through chatbot UIs.
- The environment must enforce zero retention, encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+), and appropriate regulatory controls such as HIPAA/PCI-DSS where applicable.
- If applicable, the provider should have required enterprise security terms, including BAA for relevant sensitive data use.

our UnBPO™ approach, re-engineering customer journeys, decisioning, and execution to drive better 
outcomes—not simply automate tasks.

addressable scope of the RFI, while improving cure rates, digital self-resolution, and customer experience. 
By combining GenAI, advanced analytics, and intelligent automation, we enable Comcast to move 
from static treatment strategies to dynamic, AI-orchestrated outreach—engaging customers with the 
right message, channel, and timing across the delinquency lifecycle while further reducing cost-to-
serve. 
Firstsource AI-led collections capability delivers: 
• AI-driven customer journey mapping and segmentation, leveraging behavioral, payment, and 
interaction data to tailor outreach strategies and reduce customer friction. 
• Empathetic, GenAI-powered communications, enabling personalized, compliant messaging 
across voice and digital channels to improve right-party contact and response rates. 
• Predictive and prescriptive intelligence, including propensity-to-pay and next-best-action 
models that optimize agent prioritization, channel mix, and treatment paths in real time. 
• Digital self-cure and assisted collections, through AI virtual agents and real-time agent assist, 
simplifying payment journeys and improving first-contact resolution. 
• Enterprise-grade, responsible AI governance, with built-in controls for explainability, auditability, 
and regulatory compliance—protecting Comcast’s customers and brand. 
Our flexible delivery model—combining onshore, nearshore, and offshore execution—ensures 
scalability, resilience, and continuity, while our outcome-aligned commercial construct directly ties 
investment to measurable improvements in recovery performance, customer experience, and cost-to-
serve.

expected_output:

Key solutions include **Claims as a Service (CaaS)**, QA/QC copilot, claims and provider service copilots, care gap reviews, clinical document summarization, precision member outreach, bulk inquiry resolution, risk adjustment, health risk assessment, and medication adherence.

- **Frameworks:** Firstsource uses the **4D framework** (Discover, Define, Design, Deploy), the **3P framework** (Prevent, Predict, Process), **FirstPACE 4.0** for implementation, and **FirstLearn** for workforce capability building.

- **Tools and accelerators:** Through the **relAI suite**, Firstsource offers accelerators such as **SARA Instructional Design Copilot, conversational AI, chat/call summarization, Single Pane of Glass, AI Workbench, object-centered process mining, Contract Loading Copilot, Benefits Copilot**, and healthcare-specific AI agents like **Eligibility Copilot, Clearance House AI Agent, Radiology Autonomous Coding, Smart Charge Entry Hub, and EOB Extraction**.

across all 50 states and, therefore, utilize the payor portals across all states.  Because we employ both 
onshore and offshore staff, we are able to obtain access to all requested payor portals as long as

• Medicare 
• Medicaid (all states) 
• Blue Cross/Anthem 
• Cigna 
• Humana

program/framework that Envision is putting in place? 
 
Firstsource is fully committed to supporting Envision’s vendor management program/framework.  We 
understand that Envision’s Vendor Mana gement Organization (VMO) will oversee all third -party 
vendor relationships for Envision and will be the central point of contact for Firstsource for monitoring 
contract compliance, performance metrics, invoice reconciliation, and any other business issues  
related to the Firstsource and Envision partnership.    As this program develops, we will be an active 
participant to assure its success for both Envision and Firstsource.

a. Credit balances 
i. Both government and commercial 
b. Payment posting 
c. Charge corrections 
 
Credit Balances 
 
Credit balances typically occur when payments and contractual  adjustments posted to an account 
exceed the overall total charges.   Our objective of working credit balances is to make sure our clients 
maintain compl iance, patient satisfaction, minimize the client ’s financial liability, help to properly 
state accounts receivable on their financial statements, and re solve unnecessary credit balance 
accounts that are “clogging up” the patient accounting system.

2 
 
Our work with credit balances mirrors each client’s internal polic ies and procedures for credit 
balances. Typically, our team correct s any credit balance accounts that are the r esult of misapplied 
adjustments and any credit balances that require a refund would follow the provider’s procedures for 
payment and resolution. Most providers have a policy with a threshold in place for refunds.  Note, we 
typically do not refund any payments to a patient should the patient have an outstanding balance on 
a separate account.  
 
Many credit balances are created as a result of posting errors that need to be corrected in the patient 
accounting system (GE Centricity).   If the credit balance is caused by incorrect posted allowance or 
incorrect payment estimates, Firstsource will compare reimbursement rates in the contract with the 
contractual adjustment pos ted at the time of billing and the contractual allowance amount on the 
remittance advice.   We will identify which contrac tual is correct and make the appropriate 
adjustments.   If needed, we contact the payor for payment corrections. 
 
Part of our credit balance resolution process is determining the root cause and origin of the credit 
balance.  We will make recommendations on changes to policies and procedures to avoid future credit 
balances.   If the patient credit balance is small, we typically send a notification that the credit balance 
exists along with an explanation on how to request a refund. 
 
Similar to credit balances, we will work with Envision to follow any procedures related to small balance 
write-offs for small debit balances. 
 
Throughout the engagement, Firstsource will maintain compliance with all third -party billing and 
reimbursement regulations and reimbursements and applicable federal, state, and local regulations - 
we have a rigorous audit program in place.

your specific policies (including credit balance policies) with which we must comply. These 
documented policies are als o incorporated into our training and  procedure materials for the 
engagement and made available to all our staff working on the engagement.    
 
Payment Posting 
 
Our understanding is that the Firstsource  team will run the electronic files and post 
exceptions/fallouts manually into GE Centricity as well as any lockbox, EFT and credit card payments 
and reconcile the batch totals. l f we are unable to determine where to post funds, any money that 
cannot be po sted to a patient would be posted into an unpostable account. This would be for the 
purposes to balance the deposit for that day. Additional follow up and r esearch would continue 
immediately following until the funds are properly posted .  Sometimes it is a s simple as getting an 
EOB from a payer/website. Sometimes the money is truly “not ours” and then it is applied according 
to client process/workflow. 
 
For denials posting, depending on the denial and system logic set up, the balance is moved to the 
patient or NRP at the posting level. For example: deductibles.  As soon as denials are posted through 
an ERA, those automatically become part of the denial team process to research and properly resolve 
the denial.

3 
 
We utilize a deposit log for balances and reconciliation purposes. All EFT, lockbox, credit card 
payment, etc., are captured based on the banking details. All posting is then reconciled to the deposit 
log and balanced accordingly.  Typically, our turnaround time for posting would be completed within 
2 business days from deposit details received  
 
We would contact a payor in case we did not get an EOB and there is no ERA. We would also contact 
a payor regarding offsets or take backs when the details are unclear for proper posting. 
 
 
Charge Corrections 
 
Often a claim error is the result of incorrect demographic, insurance, or charge information.  Part of 
our scope of work for Envision will include charge corrections.   We research the claim error and enter 
in correct charge information in GE Centricity.  We also correct any demographic and insurance 
information and rebill the claim.    
 
Our charge correction team does not make coding changes.   Claims that may need clinical review will 
be forwarded to our coding team to review claims for any medical record changes.   These claims will 
be submitted back to Envision to recode. 
 
As part of our charge correction work, we provide any feedback on charge capture issues and report 
these back to Envision.    
 
4. We would like to know if they have an internal minimum commitment to continuous improvement 
initiatives – i.e., Minimum number of six sigma projects to implement? 
 
Yes, Firstsource is committed to continuous improvements in all our engagements. We have, in fact, 
targeted a productivity improvement of 10% year-over-year as part of our proposed pricing model to 
Envision.  Every Firstsource engagement utilizes 1-2 Process Excellence resources who are Six Sigma 
certified to work with our Operations and Process Automation teams to drive process efficiencies on 
the engagement.  Our Six Sigma initiatives for Envision are established based on identified areas for 
continuous improvement which are reviewed and approved by the Envision and Firstsource Project 
Sponsors. The goals of each project are aligned to the goals of the engagement that are set by 
Envision. 
 
Our governance structure (see chart below) also provides for the project team to collaborate with 
Envision leaders on the shared goals of the engagement in terms of people, process, transformation, 
and financials.  
 
In 2020, we launched our Citizen Developer program to further deploy automation and accelerate the 
pace of transformation. This grass roots program has enabled employees throughout the Firstsource 
organization including those without prior programming experience, to identify and prioritize tasks

input: How are payments posted/reconciled, credits resolved, and non-coding charge errors corrected in GE Centricity?
expected_output:
Payments are handled in GE Centricity by posting electronic files, with exceptions/fallouts, lockbox, EFT, and credit card payments posted manually, then reconciling all postings to a deposit log and batch totals. If funds cannot be matched to a patient, they are temporarily posted to an unpostable account so the daily deposit balances, with follow-up research continuing until properly posted. Firstsource states posting is typically completed within 2 business days of receiving deposit details.

Credit balances are resolved by identifying the root cause, correcting posting or adjustment errors in GE Centricity, comparing contract reimbursement rates to remittance advice, and making the appropriate adjustments. If a refund is required, they follow the provider’s policies and thresholds, and generally do not refund patients if the patient has an outstanding balance on another account.

For non-coding charge errors, Firstsource researches the claim issue, corrects charge, demographic, or insurance information directly in GE Centricity, and rebills the claim. They do not make coding changes; any claims needing clinical or coding review are sent to the coding team and then returned to Envision for recoding.

balances. Typically, our team correct s any credit balance accounts that are the r esult of misapplied 
adjustments and any credit balances that require a refund would follow the provider’s procedures for 
payment and resolution. Most providers have a policy with a threshold in place for refunds.  Note, we 
typically do not refund any payments to a patient should the patient have an outstanding balance on 
a separate account.  
 
Many credit balances are created as a result of posting errors that need to be corrected in the patient 
accounting system (GE Centricity).   If the credit balance is caused by incorrect posted allowance or 
incorrect payment estimates, Firstsource will compare reimbursement rates in the contract with the 
contractual adjustment pos ted at the time of billing and the contractual allowance amount on the 
remittance advice.   We will identify which contrac tual is correct and make the appropriate 
adjustments.   If needed, we contact the payor for payment corrections. 
 
Part of our credit balance resolution process is determining the root cause and origin of the credit 
balance.  We will make recommendations on changes to policies and procedures to avoid future credit 
balances.   If the patient credit balance is small, we typically send a notification that the credit balance 
exists along with an explanation on how to request a refund. 
 
Similar to credit balances, we will work with Envision to follow any procedures related to small balance 
write-offs for small debit balances. 
 
Throughout the engagement, Firstsource will maintain compliance with all third -party billing and 
reimbursement regulations and reimbursements and applicable federal, state, and local regulations - 
we have a rigorous audit program in place.   
 
Additionally, at the start of the engagement, Firstsource will work closely with Envision to understand 
your specific policies (including credit balance policies) with which we must comply. These 
documented policies are als o incorporated into our training and  procedure materials for the 
engagement and made available to all our staff working on the engagement.    
 
Payment Posting 
 
Our understanding is that the Firstsource  team will run the electronic files and post 
exceptions/fallouts manually into GE Centricity as well as any lockbox, EFT and credit card payments 
and reconcile the batch totals. l f we are unable to determine where to post funds, any money that 
cannot be po sted to a patient would be posted into an unpostable account. This would be for the 
purposes to balance the deposit for that day. Additional follow up and r esearch would continue 
immediately following until the funds are properly posted .  Sometimes it is a s simple as getting an 
EOB from a payer/website. Sometimes the money is truly “not ours” and then it is applied according 
to client process/workflow. 
 
For denials posting, depending on the denial and system logic set up, the balance is moved to the 
patient or NRP at the posting level. For example: deductibles.  As soon as denials are posted through 
an ERA, those automatically become part of the denial team process to research and properly resolve 
the denial.

3 
 
We utilize a deposit log for balances and reconciliation purposes. All EFT, lockbox, credit card 
payment, etc., are captured based on the banking details. All posting is then reconciled to the deposit 
log and balanced accordingly.  Typically, our turnaround time for posting would be completed within 
2 business days from deposit details received  
 
We would contact a payor in case we did not get an EOB and there is no ERA. We would also contact 
a payor regarding offsets or take backs when the details are unclear for proper posting. 
 
 
Charge Corrections 
 
Often a claim error is the result of incorrect demographic, insurance, or charge information.  Part of 
our scope of work for Envision will include charge corrections.   We research the claim error and enter 
in correct charge information in GE Centricity.  We also correct any demographic and insurance 
information and rebill the claim.    
 
Our charge correction team does not make coding changes.   Claims that may need clinical review will 
be forwarded to our coding team to review claims for any medical record changes.   These claims will 
be submitted back to Envision to recode. 
 
As part of our charge correction work, we provide any feedback on charge capture issues and report 
these back to Envision.    
 
4. We would like to know if they have an internal minimum commitment to continuous improvement 
initiatives – i.e., Minimum number of six sigma projects to implement? 
 
Yes, Firstsource is committed to continuous improvements in all our engagements. We have, in fact, 
targeted a productivity improvement of 10% year-over-year as part of our proposed pricing model to 
Envision.  Every Firstsource engagement utilizes 1-2 Process Excellence resources who are Six Sigma 
certified to work with our Operations and Process Automation teams to drive process efficiencies on 
the engagement.  Our Six Sigma initiatives for Envision are established based on identified areas for 
continuous improvement which are reviewed and approved by the Envision and Firstsource Project 
Sponsors. The goals of each project are aligned to the goals of the engagement that are set by 
Envision. 
 
Our governance structure (see chart below) also provides for the project team to collaborate with 
Envision leaders on the shared goals of the engagement in terms of people, process, transformation, 
and financials.  
 
In 2020, we launched our Citizen Developer program to further deploy automation and accelerate the 
pace of transformation. This grass roots program has enabled employees throughout the Firstsource 
organization including those without prior programming experience, to identify and prioritize tasks 
ideal for automation using our Automation Hub as well as build, publish and run their own 
automations. The pilot program has been highly successful with more than 170 automation ideas and 
100+ bots created in a span of 10 weeks, adding tremendous value to our internal processes by 
reducing errors and optimizing processing time.   Firstsource is fully committed to our continued 
process and quality improvement initiatives to benefit our clients.

4

throughout our partnership with Envision.

5. What is their approach to deliverable and obligation management? 
 
Firstsource is fully committed to meeting all obligations as defined in our agreement with Envision – 
including timely completion of all deliverables.    Our approach to deliverable and obligation 
management is based on complete transparency.   For example, we expect to have daily or weekly 
meetings with Envision during the critical initial start-up, transition, and knowledge transfer period.  
Once we have achieved steady state, we will continue with weekly, bi-weekly, or monthly meetings 
to assure that all e pectations are met including all production and performance K  ’s and S  ’s. 
 
Firstsource aligns with the goals set by our clients for each individual engagement.  We believe that a 
successful partnership model is one where we have mutually aligned objectives and goals.  With both 
Envision and Firstsource being equally committed to success, it will lead to us having a better 
partnership that is more collaborative and is closely aligned because we are working toward the same 
goals.  We recommend a multi-tiered approach to this :  1.) agreed upon service level agreements 
(SLA’s) (i.e., those documented in the RFP) and 2.) key performance indicators  K  ’s  for other areas 
of productivity, performance, and quality.  This will help enable us to monitor our performance against 
e pectations and assure that Firstsource’s goals are aligned with Envision’s ob ectives.   
 
Firstsource is committed to developing S  ’s and K  ’s with Envision that will provide a scorecard for 
measuring our performance. As part of our contracting and implementation process, we will work 
with Envision to establish mutually agreed upon performance measures. Typically, our client 
partnerships include S  ’s for production productivity (i.e., number of claims worked per day), 
resolution targets (A/R resolved), collection targets, turnaround targets, and quality achievement 
targets. We believe having well defined S  ’s and K  ’s makes for a stronger and more successful 
partnership with our clients. 
 
Once operational, we monitor workloads, productivity, and account assignments very closely. When 
assigning accounts to Firstsource account representatives, our management takes into

knowledge and expertise to effectively bill insurance, overturn denials, dispute contractual 
discrepancies, work insurance accounts and thus maximize resolution and collections.  
 
Our project for Envision will be staffed based on the actual volume of accounts placed with 
Firstsource to ensure sufficient activity occurs on each account in a timely manner. In addition, 
Firstsource will allocate experienced account representatives to work Envision’ s accounts on an as-
needed basis to accommodate for increases in accounts placed. Firstsource has staffed comparable 
projects and will establish a project team for Envision composed of tenured account representatives 
and recruited staff using a skill-based methodology to designate employees for supervisory and 
support roles. 
 
We are also open to utilizing a financially driven gain-share model that will further incent Firstsource
