Table of Contents


## Organizational Background
Full name of Company
Firstsource Health Plans and Healthcare Services, LLC
Please provide a brief history of your company, the year your company was founded, location of your corporate headquarters, and number of employees.
Firstsource Solutions Limited, part of the RP Sanjiv Goenka Group, is a leading provider of customized Business Process Management (BPM), Technology, and Digital Transformation services spanning the customer lifecycle across Healthcare, Banking and Financial Services, Communications, Media, and Technology. Firstsource was established in 2001. 
We entered the healthcare segment in 2005 by acquiring MedAssist, a healthcare company that started in 1993. Firstsource Transaction Services, LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Firstsource Solutions USA, LLC.  was incorporated under the State of Delaware laws on May 26, 2011, as a full-fledged healthcare arm of Firstsource Solutions. In October 2020, the Firstsource Healthcare Payer division was rebranded as Firstsource Health Plans & Healthcare Services.
Firstsource is headquartered in Louisville, Kentucky, with facilities present globally in 6 countries at both onshore and offshore locations. 28,000+ employees deliver “moments that matter” from facilities across 48 global delivery centers.
How long have you been established at the proposed site for claims processing services?
Firstsource Healthcare offers claims services from its India delivery centers in Chennai, Trichy, Hyderabad, Bangalore, etc., and its US service centers in Chattanooga, Tennessee; Salt Lake City, Utah; Dallas, Texas; Rockford, Illinois; Kentucky; and Kansas, etc. Firstsource plans to deliver the Claims processing service outlined in this RFP from our Offshore India locations - Chennai and Hyderabad. 
Chennai Delivery Center and Process Mining Center of Excellence 
Operational since: 2016 | Build-Up Area: 69,700 Sq. Ft | Seats: 2,500+
Current Services/Support at the Location: Claims Intake, Claims adjudication and adjustment, Provider Data Management, Digital Intake, Enrolment, Membership Billing, and Configuration.
Hyderabad Delivery Center
Operational since: 2021 | Build-Up Area: 72,229 Sq. Ft and 55,650 Sq. Ft | Seats: 2,000+
Current Services/Support at the Location: Claims Adjudication and Adjustments, Provider Data Management, Order Management, Invoice processing, and Provider Revenue Cycle Management.
For additional details on our Offshore delivery centers, please refer to the “Locations” section below.
Please provide a list of current healthcare payers that you provide claims processing services for.
Firstsource Healthcare currently has more than 4,640+ experienced claims examiners processing 55M claims and 1.3 M+ Appeals & Grievance cases annually for 20 Health Plans, including 6 of the top 10 Health Plans in the US:
A Fortune 500, multi-state health care organization – Provider claims resolution for Commercial and Medicaid LOB with multiple scenarios, reprocessing of incorrectly processed claims
One of the largest Medicaid managed care plans in the U.S serving >2M members – Claims Adjustment fallout and rework, Appeals & Grievances, provider letter generation.
A Top # 5 National Health Plan - Claims Processing on CAMS, Facets, and UNET platforms, Consumer Driven Health Plans, Combined Accumulation Reconciliation Processs
A Top # 15 multi-state Medicare and Medicaid Plan – Claims Processing, Grievances and Appeals, Member and Provider Services, Digital Intake. 
One of the largest Blue Plans with >40M members - Claims Processing and Provider Operations
An American-managed Health care company - Medicaid Claims Processing, handling XC claims for HMO and PPO Health Plans.
A leading not-for-profit plan in Hawaii – entire back-office in a BPaaS model including Claims, Enrollment & Billing, Provider Data Management, and Provider Calls across Commercial, Medicare, and Medicaid Lines of Business.
A leading East Coast-based BCBS Plan - Managing government and commercial claims adjudication and data entry support lines of business, 2.7M+ per annum volumes processed. 
A subsidiary of one of the top 5 leading Blues Health Plans – Claims processing, Enrollment out of offshore location in India. 
For more details on our Claims Operations, please refer to this document's “Experience” section.
Please state the name, title, address, telephone number and e-mail address of the primary RFP contact(s) we may reach out to with any questions regarding your response.
Name: Rajesh Reddy
Title: VP, Client Services, Firstsource Solutions Ltd.
Address: 10400 Linn Station Road, Suite 215 Louisville, KY 40223 
E-mail:  Rajesh.Reddy@firstsource.com
Phone No.: +1 757 632 1532
Does your organization have any pending mergers, acquisitions, or alliances that might affect its service delivery to Humana?  If so, provide details.
We do not have any pending mergers, acquisitions, or alliances that might affect our service delivery to Humana.
Are you a certified Diversity Vendor (i.e., Minority Business Enterprise (MBE), Woman Owned Business Enterprise (WBE), Small Business Enterprise (SBE), Disadvantaged, Veteran, Disabled, Disabled Veteran, HUBZONE, Vietnam Veteran, etc.?  Please mention all that are applicable. In the Comment Field, indicate the approximate percent of business for each type of Diversity Vendor that applies.
Firstsource is an equal opportunity employer, and we promote diversity in our teams and partner ecosystem. While we are not certified as a diversity vendor, we actively seek opportunities to work with MWBE organizations. Our existing client engagements participate in their MWDVBE program and have committed some of our delivery services to partner with MWDVE companies.
Firstsource, for the second successive year, has been recognized by the Bloomberg Gender-Equality Index (GEI), 2023, as an organization committed to transparency in gender-data reporting and creating a workplace conducive for diverse talent to succeed.
If you are a certified Diversity Vendor, list certification groups here and attach your current certificate.
Not applicable


## 2. Locations
What is the address of the location(s) where the Claims Research and Resolution Processing services will be located?   
Firstsource plans to deliver the Claims research and resolution services outlined in this RFP from our Onshore and Offshore locations for Medicaid and Medicare LOB, respectively. For the Onshore, US, we have considered Work from Home, and for Offshore, we are proposing Chennai and Hyderabad delivery centers in India. However, we are open to discussing other options if Humana wishes to choose one of our other offshore delivery centers. 
Chennai Facility
Operational since: 2016
Address 1: Block 4, 5th floor, Sandhya Infocity Limited, 33 Old Mahabalipuram Road, Navallur village, Kancheepuram District, Chennai, 603103
Address 2: Ozone Techno Park, 1/13, Old Mahabalipuram Rd, Navallur, Chennai, Tamil Nadu 603103
Hyderabad Facility
Operational since: 2021
Address: 1st and 5th Floor, Block 1 survey No. 142, Nanakramguda Village, Serilingampally Mandal & Municipality Ranga Reddy District, Hyderabad GHMC 500008.
We have selected these locations based on below parameters:
Talent Availability: Chennai and Hyderabad have abundant talent with US healthcare claims experience.
Experienced and qualified workforce: Our teams in Hyderabad and Chennai have extensive experience in claims operations and will be used as seed teams for Humana operations. 
Strong Leadership talent: Firstsource has tenured healthcare leadership to support this program.
Robust infrastructure: Our delivery centers in Hyderabad and Chennai have the latest technology and infrastructure to support claims operations. This includes high-speed internet, state-of-the-art data centers, and a secure environment.
In addition, we recommend leveraging a blended ‘Work at Home’ strategy to attract and retain talent. Our strategy is to:
Hire and train resources in the office. 
Once employees have attained the required proficiency and demonstrated targeted performance, allow them to work from home.
An option to bring the employees back to the office if necessary to manage the performance. 
Please explain your offshore capabilities and locations. What does success look like at these locations?
Firstsource has 5 Claims Centers of Excellence (CoE) in India – Chennai, Hyderabad, Trichy, Bangalore and Vijayawada. We invite you to visit the proposed Firstsource locations virtually. The facilities are equipped with Fire Suppression systems, UPS systems, CCTV, and ergonomic work area:
Figure 1:Real-time view of the system up-time and availability
We measure our success at these locations based on the below criteria –
High customer satisfaction – Customers should be satisfied with the quality of service they receive. 
Longevity of the customer partnership – The average tenure of our customers is 14 years, more than 60% of our growth in the last 5 years is contributed by our existing customers and we have not had any terminations due to performance in the last 10 years.
On-time and accurate performance – All SLAs / KPIs are monitored frequently, and actions are taken to improve performance. The goal is to meet and exceed all SLAs and KPIs.
Continuous improvement – Continuous improvement across all the metrics by leveraging technology to reduce costs and increase customer and employee satisfaction.
Employee Satisfaction and Retention rates – We conduct periodic employee satisfaction surveys to seek feedback from our employees and take actions to improve satisfaction that helps improve our retention rate.
Please explain your nearshore capabilities and locations. What does success look like at these locations?
Firstsource has a nearshore presence delivering contact center operations in Colombia, and Mexico. We primarily deliver contact center services including member and provider queries for our Health Plan customers from these centers.
We do not recommend nearshore delivery for claims operations from a cost and talent perspective.
Please explain your onshore capabilities and locations. What does success look like at these locations?
Firstsource Healthcare offers claims services from its US service centers in Chattanooga, Tennessee; Salt Lake City, Utah; Dallas, Texas; Rockford, Illinois, Kentucky, Florida; and Kansas, etc. Most of our claims associates Onshore are working from home; however, we are well equipped in terms of infrastructure and other resources to have the associates work in a B&M model or hybrid WAH as per your requirement. These service centers are strategically located in areas with abundant highly skilled staff in low-cost markets.
We measure our engagement success based on the below criteria –
High customer satisfaction – Customers should be satisfied with the quality of service they receive. 
Longevity of the customer partnership – The average tenure of our customers is 14 years, more than 60% of our growth in the last 5 years is contributed by our existing customers and we have not had any terminations due to performance in the last 10 years.
On-time and accurate performance – All SLAs / KPIs are monitored frequently, and actions are taken to improve performance. The goal is to meet and exceed all SLAs and KPIs.
Continuous improvement – Continuous improvement across all the metrics by leveraging technology to reduce costs and increase customer and employee satisfaction.
Employee Satisfaction and Retention rates – We conduct periodic employee satisfaction surveys to seek feedback from our employees and take actions to improve satisfaction that helps improve our retention rate.


## Service Levels
How do you plan to staff to manage peak volume? What are your plans/strategy for managing peak volumes? What SLAs would you recommend for managing this work in addition to the SLAs defined in the Requirements?
Firstsource has a standardized global approach to Workforce Management. We use consistent processes across all centers and geographies for forecasting, workforce planning, and scheduling practices considering local geographic dynamics, such as holidays, recruitment timelines, and training timelines. This strategy helped us manage the peak volumes effectively; for example, for one of our large customers, we increased the staffing by 50% (400 additional employees) to work the peak volume between October and February of every year. For another customer, due to their nature of business, we add staffing to manage the additional volume during the holidays (Spring break, Summer, Christmas, and Thanksgiving). 
Firstsource has effective strategies to deal with Service Level Management. One of the key factors is the variations in the volumes of our clients. To deal with peaks and troughs, we use long-term forecasting. Peaks and troughs occur because of seasonality. We engage with our clients to understand their volume forecast for a couple of months, and we ensure that we hire the right number of people, keeping in mind the training time, upskilling, etc. 
Here are additional details about our Workforce Management approach:
We use a variety of data sources to forecast demand, including historical data, customer feedback, and market trends.
We use a variety of scheduling algorithms to optimize our workforce, including rule-based scheduling, optimization-based scheduling, and self-scheduling.
We have a robust training and development program to ensure that our employees have the skills and knowledge they need to be successful.
We strongly focus on employee engagement and well-being, which helps us attract and retain top talent.
We believe our Workforce Management approach is one of the best in the industry. It helps us deliver high-quality customer service while managing our costs effectively.
Core-Flex Model to address the volume fluctuations and seasonality during the steady-state operations.
Additionally, the seasonal nature of the work requires Firstsource to maintain a flexible staffing model with a high level of accuracy and competency to succeed. Firstsource utilizes a core-flex model to quickly ramp up and down to manage the volume fluctuations while retaining the core process and system knowledge. For the scope of service in this RFP, which has volume fluctuations, we will implement the same model to ramp up and down based on the volume spike quickly. 
Figure 3: Managing Volume Fluctuations Effectively with Core-Flex Model
We plan for resources to meet future demand through detailed forecasting and capacity planning. 
Redeploy and cross-train resources.
Overtime and managing shrinkage to address short-term needs.
Plan and train resources to ensure the capacity is always maintained to address shortfalls due to attrition.
Maintain buffer staff to manage unforeseen attrition and unexpected volume spikes.
Robust hiring pipeline to quickly hire and train resources.
We developed a strong SLA management process by leveraging our experience in delivering best-in-class services to various customers. 
What is your strategy for meeting service levels? Please also provide a corrective action plan for situations when you fall behind SLAs.
Firstsource has a robust Service Level Management Program, designed, and augmented with Smart audit solutions, Continuous performance monitoring, and side-by-side coaching, which help us achieve target KPIs. We have built-in business validations/rules within the existing process for all projects that ensure the quality is controlled, measured, and delivered as per the Service Level Agreement. Our tenure with our clients is not only long-term but has evolved and expanded over the years as we have continued to improve operational effectiveness and customer experience for our client partners.
Below are highlights of our SLA management process:
Establish SLAs and KPIs – this includes both the client SLAs / KPIs from the agreement and internal SLAs / KPIs. For example, Accuracy, TAT (Client SLAs) & Attrition, Shrinkage, Schedule Adherence, and Training Throughput (Internal SLAs).
Tracking and Reporting – Implement measurement criteria and frequency for each SLA / KPI and publish comprehensive reports to track performance against goals.
Identify potential SLA failures –Identify SLAs falling behind the goals and trending in the wrong direction, please refer to the ‘Reporting’ section.

Please outline your trainer selection process. Additionally how do you ensure trainers are vetted for their performance and ability to relate, and constructively engage, with trainees.
We have in-house trainers with significant years of industry and training experience. The training is performed in designated classrooms (Physical and Virtual) at timings that map the client's requirements. We have a robust succession planning structure facilitating quick resource movements to critical programs. 
Trainer Certifications
Firstsource trainers are certified by a 2-step process; internal and external. During Train the Trainer (TTT) process, trainers are coached on the fundamentals of teaching material, introductory presentation, escalation handling, etc. The Firstsource trainer is then placed into a live training class where both Humana and the internal Training Coordinator will evaluate and certify them separately. After being certified both by the Internal coordinator and Humana trainer, the trainer will be equipped to independently train, evaluate, and approve new hires. We also have an alternate process where we ask the Humana trainer to monitor through a remote system and audit a sample set of interactions done by the Firstsource trainer. Based on the quality of those interactions, the latter is evaluated and certified by a Humana trainer.
Train the Trainer Approach
Step 1: Trainer Identification
Experienced knowledge champions lead the KT process.
Firstsource to identify trainers based on the following:
Facilitation skills
Effective presentation skills
SOP writing
Content and assessment creation
Step 2: Knowledge Transfer
Firstsource trainers will undergo process training along with pilot batch associates and complete the certification process based on Humana’s passing threshold or through exclusive Train-the-Trainer sessions conducted by Humana.
Humana subject matter experts will certify the Firstsource trainers based on the live teach-back sessions with a passing threshold of 80%.
Humana’s e-mail confirmation will support that the trainer is "Good to Go, " along with the certification results.
The certified trainers and the associates will continue to work on live cases to understand the process in depth through the steady state.
Firstsource trainers will act as mentors for the existing batch of trainees, clarifying their questions and helping them when they are stuck during the ramp phase.
Firstsource trainers will handle the subsequent batches independently, with Humana trainers remotely monitoring the first few sessions.

What do you consider best in class auditing for Claims Research and Resolution Processing services?
Firstsource Claims audit team follows a 4-stage process to ensure best-in-class audits are delivered from the inception of the program.
Stage 1: Unbiased & System driven sampling methodology
The sampling is picked based on “All types of transactions for all agents.” This is done based on client specifications and or COPC sampling methodology. We identify the Transaction types within the scope of the engagement that need to be audited, linking them with agreed service level metrics and the compliance requirements through identified process parameters and outcome-based measures. The statistically arriving samples are stratified across, and additional audits would be conducted for New Hires and focus audits on exceptional transactions (High dollar audits, Sub-Par performers, etc.)
Stage 2: Recording audits & Timely reporting 
Audits are recorded in the Firstsource proprietary system (Sympraxis) or any system provided by the client to ensure data is stored and retrieved based on the program's needs. The audits are completed based on the processor and examiner/process SOPs, and any deviation from the process is captured for feedback. The feedback may be sourced to a system, process, or individual, and the feedback is shared with appropriate teams to ensure that appropriate action is taken.
Using the multiple data cuts available from the reports generated by Firstsource’s proprietary system, accurate and effective reporting  will be published to Humana.
These reports have multiple levels of information related to overall program quality, individual agent level quality, day-wise, week-wise, month-wise, and High Dollar. A separate level of analysis will be circulated for top defect categories and a 2 X 2 matrix or Box plot to showcase agents vs. error categories comparison.
Stage 3: Coaching & Defects Remediation plan
Quality auditors perform 1-0-1 coaching to agents on the same day. Errors are discussed through the daily quality huddle platform to create awareness among the entire team about the defects. Defect categories are grouped based on RCA and brainstorming exercises. QAs will jot down remediation plans for the agents and their defects periodically.
Rebuttals
In the event of Rebuttals, they are supposed to be communicated within 1 business day of the defect being assessed. Rebuttals are submitted through the rebuttal central repository which is monitored by senior auditors daily. Senior Quality Auditors review and respond to rebuttals with uphold or overturn decisions based on the applicable process within 1 business day of receipt. Notification is sent to the operations associates or applicable parties automatically.
Rebuttals are expected to be reviewed within the timeframe regardless of PTO. If PTO is a factor, the expectation is to ensure there is adequate coverage of rebuttals. The operations supervisor will review the rebuttal decision and either coach/provide feedback to the associate accordingly or escalate to their leader if they disagree. If a rebuttal decision is still disagreed upon after escalation to the leader, the leader will reach out to the quality supervisor to discuss and calibrate. The calibrated decision is final. 
Rebuttals must be complete and include all applicable policies/procedure references. Rebuttals must be void of all personal content and inflammatory language.   They must be professional and factual.  Any rebuttal containing inflammatory language or personal content may be subject to corrective action.  Rebuttals lacking sufficient information for evaluation are upheld. Operations are responsible for determining the responsible parties for reviewing rebuttals. Overturned rebuttals are tracked and used for performance measurement for quality auditors and rollup to leaders. 
Stage 4: Calibrating the knowledge of auditors
Periodic internal and Client audit calibration exercises to ensure all auditors stay on top of their audit skills, efficiencies, and procedures. Any discrepancies in the auditor’s performance will be dealt through appropriate coaching and Training.

What do you consider best in class auditing for Claims Research and Resolution Processing services?
Firstsource Claims audit team follows a 4-stage process to ensure best-in-class audits are delivered from the inception of the program.
Stage 1: Unbiased & System driven sampling methodology
The sampling is picked based on “All types of transactions for all agents.” This is done based on client specifications and or COPC sampling methodology. We identify the Transaction types within the scope of the engagement that need to be audited, linking them with agreed service level metrics and the compliance requirements through identified process parameters and outcome-based measures. The statistically arriving samples are stratified across, and additional audits would be conducted for New Hires and focus audits on exceptional transactions (High dollar audits, Sub-Par performers, etc.)
Stage 2: Recording audits & Timely reporting 
Audits are recorded in the Firstsource proprietary system (Sympraxis) or any system provided by the client to ensure data is stored and retrieved based on the program's needs. The audits are completed based on the processor and examiner/process SOPs, and any deviation from the process is captured for feedback. The feedback may be sourced to a system, process, or individual, and the feedback is shared with appropriate teams to ensure that appropriate action is taken.
Using the multiple data cuts available from the reports generated by Firstsource’s proprietary system, accurate and effective reporting  will be published to Humana.
These reports have multiple levels of information related to overall program quality, individual agent level quality, day-wise, week-wise, month-wise, and High Dollar. A separate level of analysis will be circulated for top defect categories and a 2 X 2 matrix or Box plot to showcase agents vs. error categories comparison.
Stage 3: Coaching & Defects Remediation plan
Quality auditors perform 1-0-1 coaching to agents on the same day. Errors are discussed through the daily quality huddle platform to create awareness among the entire team about the defects. Defect categories are grouped based on RCA and brainstorming exercises. QAs will jot down remediation plans for the agents and their defects periodically.
Rebuttals
In the event of Rebuttals, they are supposed to be communicated within 1 business day of the defect being assessed. Rebuttals are submitted through the rebuttal central repository which is monitored by senior auditors daily. Senior Quality Auditors review and respond to rebuttals with uphold or overturn decisions based on the applicable process within 1 business day of receipt. Notification is sent to the operations associates or applicable parties automatically.
Rebuttals are expected to be reviewed within the timeframe regardless of PTO. If PTO is a factor, the expectation is to ensure there is adequate coverage of rebuttals. The operations supervisor will review the rebuttal decision and either coach/provide feedback to the associate accordingly or escalate to their leader if they disagree. If a rebuttal decision is still disagreed upon after escalation to the leader, the leader will reach out to the quality supervisor to discuss and calibrate. The calibrated decision is final. 
Rebuttals must be complete and include all applicable policies/procedure references. Rebuttals must be void of all personal content and inflammatory language.   They must be professional and factual.  Any rebuttal containing inflammatory language or personal content may be subject to corrective action.  Rebuttals lacking sufficient information for evaluation are upheld. Operations are responsible for determining the responsible parties for reviewing rebuttals. Overturned rebuttals are tracked and used for performance measurement for quality auditors and rollup to leaders. 
Stage 4: Calibrating the knowledge of auditors
Periodic internal and Client audit calibration exercises to ensure all auditors stay on top of their audit skills, efficiencies, and procedures. Any discrepancies in the auditor’s performance will be dealt through appropriate coaching and Training.

## Operational Questions:


## What are your operational hours for customer care and telesales support? Are you able to handle 24/7 operations?
Our sites can run 24/7 operations, ensuring that all critical processes and client needs are met without interruption. Our sites have the necessary infrastructure and workforce management strategies to ensure continuous operations, catering to the requirements of our clients across different time zones. We have a robust staffing plan, with teams scheduled to work in shifts to cover all hours, including nights, weekends, and public holidays, for a few of our clients at these sites. Our technical support and IT infrastructure are designed to function seamlessly around the clock, providing necessary support whenever required.


## How do you ensure coverage during peak times, weekends, and holidays?
We have extensive experience managing peaks; our large client base and robust planning and recruitment engine allow us to repurpose and redeploy our colleagues to provide flexibility.
Fig.7: Scaling and flexing
At Firstsource, our workforce management includes dedicated teams for planning, forecasting, scheduling, and real-time adherence. These experts handle accounts' forecasting, planning, and scheduling, using platforms like NICE and VERINT to provide accurate forecasts and optimised schedules.
Schedules are planned weekly for the next 1-4 weeks, using locked forecasts and agent input. Agents can choose their preferred shifts and days off, reducing shrinkage and attrition. Once finalised, schedules are available on a remote platform and are accessible via desktop or mobile devices as per client agreements.
Volume management
Firstsource will be responsible for staffing at appropriate levels to meet the service requirements. We understand that there will be planned activities that may drive volumes up and other seasonal spikes that we foresee for certain months of the year. While all the planned volume fluctuations (seasonal spikes) will be managed through a robust change management programme, the sudden spikes in the intraday volume (while running any campaigns/ events) or at short notice during the week will be managed differently in real-time. 
For peak hour staffing needs, managers utilise dedicated employees who are available but not scheduled to work (often called ‘jumpers’). They will immediately log on to take calls. 
Onsite agents, team leaders, and quality analysts are needed to manage sudden volume spikes. 
Work at Home agents with flexible shift timings and weekend staffing -This ability to immediately flex staffing by 10-15% is possible in a virtual workforce (work at home) as employees need not commute to the office and are more willing to work in smaller shift segments. 
When too many people are scheduled, managers can ask volunteers to log off until needed.
Holiday season peak volume management
Hire temporary resources and part-timers through seasonal sourcing channels, i.e., temporary recruitment centres, the web, direct hire, social media recruitment, and tie-ups with universities to onboard students for a brief period. 
Extra login hours through stretch shifts, off-day working incentives and optimised leave management. 
Cross-training across processes: In the long run, cross-training staff across processes of a single client. This helps mitigate the risk of unknown volume split between various processes.
Shrinkage
In the context of customer service, Workforce Management (WFM) plays a vital role in aligning customer demand with the labour supply. A key aspect of WFM is the management of shrinkage, which refers to the portion of work hours where staff are on the clock but not directly engaged in customer interactions. This includes time allocated for breaks, training sessions, team meetings, and other non-call activities.


## What is your process for recruiting, training, and retaining staff for customer care and telesales roles?
Firstsource has a well-designed and proven recruitment strategy, methodology and processes to ensure that we hire the right profiles with the requisite skill sets and who will be ‘brand ambassadors’ for our clients and Firstsource with induction. The strategy is not just to hire the right talent, but it is an entirely seamless process of attracting, assessing, acquiring and acclimatising/inducting the right talent. 
Fig 8: Our global recruitment strategy
Firstsource employs a multi-channel sourcing approach to ensure we can swiftly select the best candidates from all the accessible sources. Our talent acquisition strategy blends our globalised talent practices with local talent requirements. We will also capitalise on these proven sourcing channels to recruit for the Lyca account. 
For external recruits, we will use the following sourcing channels:
Jobs boards: we actively engage with leading job boards for respective geographies to cast a wide net and reach potential candidates. Our global LinkedIn licences give us access to the talent pool available globally.
Employee referrals: we will initiate a global employee referral programme to inform all our employees about our launch and share referrals for all relevant geos. Our referral programme will be built around monetary benefits and branded merchandise that will help us further in our branding efforts.
Recruitment agencies: we would leverage our association with our current recruitment partners across the globe. Furthermore, we have established relations with leading agencies. This is often our primary sourcing channel during the initial phase, and our dependency on this channel reduces as we move towards an in-house recruitment model. 
Government/NGO agencies: we often associate with local NGOs or government agencies that work for the communities. This helps us build a local brand and makes us ‘the Employer of choice’ for members of these communities. 
Social media: We strategically leverage social platforms like LinkedIn, Instagram, and Facebook, allowing us to engage with and recruit top-tier candidates effectively. Instagram and Meta have many worldwide city- and region-specific groups for job seekers. Our expert social media recruiters will tap into these sources to maximise contribution. 
Local events: we will conduct or participate in events at public places to build our brand and attract the right talent.
Campus/universities: we have established strategic partnerships with academic institutions to facilitate campus recruitment initiatives, providing us access to a steady flow of early-career talent where the students are trained during their final year of graduation for the role.
Detailed recruitment process steps:
Step-1: HR screening
After calibration, the recruiter begins screening profiles received against the JD and calibration inputs to shortlist candidates. Post-screening, the recruiter speaks to the candidates to validate the details mentioned in the resumé. Selected resumés by the recruiter are put forward for further rounds.
Step-2: Preliminary screening
The next step is a preliminary check of the candidate’s communication skills. This is done through:
Voice support screening: The HR team conducts an initial screening round, termed Free Speech Activity (FSA), to comprehensively assess each candidate's skills, experience, and overall fit for the role. 
Messaging support screening: Typing test and conversational/situational writing is our initial screening methodology for instant messaging processes. 
Step-3: Technical assessment
Depending on the role and JD, we implement a comprehensive array of assessments to evaluate each candidate's suitability for the role thoroughly. 
Step- 4: Functional round/ Operations round
The operations/functional manager will conduct the next round of discussion. This further ascertains the candidate’s fitment in a particular role regarding skills and attitude. This round captures the remarks and final status of the candidate for evaluation. The evaluation process of this round differs based on the hiring manager's preferences.
Step-5: HR discussion
The HR discussion is conducted to evaluate a candidate on various competencies like stability, teamwork, process fitment, flexibility, and willingness to learn. The candidate is evaluated on these competencies, and the recruiter ascertains the compensation and job profile expectations. The recruiter engages in an extensive competency-based interview process with the candidate. Once a candidate clears all the above stages of selection, a final HR discussion takes place to take a final call on the candidate’s selection status. Issues related to salary, company policies, joining date, etc, are addressed, and a final decision on their selection is taken. The candidate is issued a Letter of Intent, which states that the final offer letter is conditional to the candidate, who must provide all the documents on time to the company's satisfaction. They would then receive their offer/appointment letters and be ready for onboarding.
Step-6: Background verification
After the successful completion of documentation formalities and offer acceptance on SAP SuccessFactors, the background verification is initiated for the candidate as per the client’s requirements. 
Step-7: Onboarding and induction
Depending on the date of joining assigned to the candidate, an induction is designed for the candidate to get oriented to the Firstsource environment. The induction covers the corporate overview, which gives our senior leadership members detailed insight into Firstsource’s service offerings, followed by an HR overview, which talks about performance, talent management, policies and processes, and various tools employees use daily.
As mentioned, we have immense experience in sourcing and recruiting the right profiles for Telecom and Media companies like Lyca. Our recruiters are experienced in selecting the right personas with the requisite skill sets, aptitude, and attitude to imbibe Lyca's culture and values.
The minimum experience levels required can vary from process to process based on client requirements. We will work with Lyca to determine the JD, minimum educational qualification, and experience needed before finalising and starting the recruitment process.
Training:
Our training process is designed to onboard new staff seamlessly into the organisation. The training approach focuses on customised content design and delivery that will be mapped to our client’s business objectives, customer demographics and needs, compliance requirements, service channels and Agent skill sets.
All the new hires go through a day-long induction programme to get oriented to Firstsource as an organisation and our values and ethos. Besides the client-specific product and process training, new hires will undergo culture and soft skills training (specific to nearshore and offshore locations) and Firstsource compliance training. 
Content design and delivery are two pillars that support new hires and ongoing learning:
Content design: Our content CoE (Centre of Excellence) team partners with the delivery team to understand content design requirements and uses a range of best-in-class skills, tools and technologies to create a truly immersive and transformative learning experience ranging from AR to e-learning, virtual simulations, games, videos and microlearning.

AR-powered simulations
Virtual task/call simulations that bring together soft skills, system proficiency and product knowledge
Online scenario/story-based learning

Online system simulations with “Show,” “Try,” and “Test” modes.
Gamification

All the training is delivered through a blend of Instructor-led sessions and e-learning. The success of the training is tracked and measured through periodic assessments built into the course across all stages. The below graphic outlines our training framework:

Certification and speed to proficiency
Formative and summative assessments are rolled out at the end of each stage of training to assess staff knowledge. These are tollgates to ensure only competent staff move to the next stage. All tollgates are defined and agreed upon with the client.
Accreditation occurs for both soft skills and process training, with proficiency in each case established via formative and summative proficiency tests at the end of each module.

Staff begin live interactions with customers.
Facilitator support provided.
Microlearning content for refresher based on Training Needs Identification (TNI).
Scorecard-based certification.
Step-up approach jointly owned by operations and training teams.
Ongoing performance reviews.
Graduations and gamified assessments.

Retention Amplified

## How do you ensure that your agents are proficient in English and have the necessary communication skills?
All resources will be evaluated to meet verbal and written English proficiency levels to ensure that the agents are proficient in English and have the necessary communication skills. 
Language test: successful candidates from the initial screening phase proceed to complete the comprehensive language assessment. We use SHL to assess this skill. Although the applicant's language proficiency is evaluated at various interview stages, applicants must also clear their language proficiency test. This assessment scores applicants on pronunciation, fluency, active listening, spoken English comprehension, vocabulary and grammar and is rated on CEFR parameters. The report also rates candidates on job suitability, involving direct customer interaction, international voice, domestic, and backend processing profiles. 
Instant messaging test: candidates engage with our process trainers to demonstrate their written English, customer support scenario handling, and empathy —essential for customer service roles. We use SHL/Zenerate AI Coach assessments to conduct this round and record the scores on the CEFR framework. 
Typing test: we administer a typing test that evaluates candidates' accuracy and speed, which is crucial for roles requiring efficient data entry and documentation. We again use the SHL assessment tool. 
Personality assessment provides insight into candidates' inherent traits and behavioural tendencies. We again use the SHL assessment tool. 
Skill alignment and conversation ability test:  we plan to use AI Coach, which supports skills assessment by creating role-plays based on specific skills such as sales, service, faults, collections, etc. This will enhance screening for skill-associated capabilities and conversational abilities of agents, which we believe is a current challenge area for offshore operations 
This multifaceted testing approach enables us to identify candidates with the linguistic, technical, interpersonal, and conversational skills necessary to excel within our organisation.

We have built-in systems and processes for all projects with our clients to ensure that the quality is measured and delivered as per the Service Level Agreement. Firstsource believes that quality management is a journey without a destination and quality improvement is a continuous process. These businesses focus on tailored training, error prediction, error reduction, and knowledge management improvements. Proprietary automated tools are used to track and monitor productivity and quality at an agent level. Six Sigma supports Firstsource as a quality improvement program, metrics as the basis for quality improvement, and employee participation to collectively achieve quality goals as the mission. This results in reduced waste, improved efficiency, predictable processes, and better outcomes for our clients. Key pillars in the approach include:
Business validations (QA check) - mistake-proofing solutions for the entire population
Automated control reports to monitor process mismatches
Proprietary automated tools for tracking and monitoring productivity and quality at Agent levels
Quality certification requirements based on quality thresholds for new hire training as well as upskill
Multiple/regular touchpoints with clients, operations and support functions for quick and efficient actions, including calibration and remediation activities
Integrated indigenously developed sampling methodology based on statistical sampling using COPC guidelines coupled with other sampling methods like risk-based, focused, OJT/ramp, focused, Performance Guarantee, Statistical and compliance.
Periodic leadership and client reviews on Quality performance to showcase performance trends, error analysis and remediation plans
Bottom Quartile management framework to focus on performance improvement by providing required support.

Quality check methodology
Based on the client's needs and regulatory requirements, our QA team will adopt multiple approaches to ensure all clients achieve their desired business goals. Teams will monitor a minimum number of contacts per Agent per week with an increased monitoring sample for Agents who require additional support.
This can be carried out in various ways:
Routine monitoring: Calls will be picked to assess the service quality of agents, who will be selected at random within the live week to reflect the customer service provided accurately. The sample monitored is representative of the population and covers all Agents within the week/month. The Graded monitoring approach ensures intensive coaching/feedback for 3rd and 4th quartile Agents.
Precision monitoring: This is conducted weekly to check adherence to behavioural and regulatory metrics highlighting errors. This monitoring is dynamic, with topics decided depending on the need of the process/operational focus areas for a particular month. A decision on the areas where precision checks are needed is made in consultation with our clients.
Then, the fundamental quality concepts PDCA (Plan, Do, Check, and Act) and SDCA (Standardise, Do, and Act) will form the basis of our day-to-day operational delivery.
Firstsource quality monitoring framework measures and reports Agents, team, and process level performance using: 
Process quality score – an overall score that is further broken down to accuracy scores for customer service, procedural adherence and compliance 
Fatal error/high risk %
CSAT and NPS
First Contact Resolution (FCR) percentage
Precision monitoring error %

Recognition and reward programmes: Our recognition and reward programmes celebrate the compelling achievements of our employees and foster a performance-driven culture. This motivates high-performing employees and promotes an overall standard of excellence by encouraging others to go the extra mile. 


## Can you provide examples of how you’ve handled challenging customer scenarios in the past?
Firstsource has a strong record of accomplishment of effectively managing challenging customer scenarios. 
Handling high call volumes: During peak times, we have implemented advanced call routing and automated systems to manage high call volumes efficiently. This ensures that customers receive timely assistance without long wait times, improving overall customer satisfaction 
Resolving complex issues: We have trained our customer service agents to handle complex problems by providing comprehensive training and access to a robust knowledge base. This enables them to resolve customer queries quickly and accurately, even when dealing with intricate problems 
Managing demanding customers: We have employed active listening, empathy, and clear communication strategies to manage demanding customers. By understanding the customer's perspective and addressing their concerns promptly, Firstsource has been able to turn potentially harmful experiences into positive ones 
Adapting to regulatory changes: While working with the financial services sector, we have successfully navigated regulatory changes by staying updated with the latest compliance requirements and training its staff accordingly. This proactive approach ensures that customers receive accurate and compliant services. 
A few more examples to highlight our commitment to delivering exceptional customer service, even in challenging situations, are as follows: 
Price increase scenario: The price increase for Broadband and TV service customers in the UK happens annually around April and is primarily attributed to rising inflation. This means that the cost of providing these services increases, influencing companies to pass on some of those costs to the customers. This has several impacts on the customers, like increased monthly bills and reduced disposable income, leading to customers either looking to cancel their services or look for cheaper alternative providers. This is the most challenging time for the advisors as we see an influx of customers expressing their intent to cancel their service with us due to the Price Increase (between February and April). We empathise with the customer and then profile them to identify if the existing packages/services we offer cater to the customer’s needs and preferences while constantly highlighting the brand value of the company we represent. We tailor their requirement with offers where available to enhance value and potentially retain these customers. 
Payment-related concerns on outbound calls impacting sales: A significant portion of our customer base expressed reluctance to share their bank details for setting up direct debit payments, hindering the adoption of this convenient payment method. This resulted in a lower-than-expected uptake of direct debit and increased reliance on less efficient payment methods. The primary challenge was a payment-related issue stemming from customers’ distrust and concerns regarding the security of sharing sensitive financial information, thus negatively closing a sale. We developed a robust objection handling statement to address customers’ concerns regarding direct debit security. This statement emphasised: 
Transparency and control: Explaining how customers retain complete control over their direct debit payments, including the ability to cancel or modify them at any time.  
Benefits of direct debit: Highlighting the convenience and reliability of direct debit, including automated payments, avoiding late fees, and simplifying fiscal management.   
Addressing specific concerns: Providing agents with scripts to address common objections, such as fears of unauthorised transactions or data breaches.


## What is your approach to customer retention and upselling during telesales calls?
Our telesales strategy maximises customer value and long-term retention through a data-driven approach. Key elements of our approach include
Proactive Retention – We use predictive analytics to identify at-risk customers early, addressing concerns with personalised solutions and retention offers
Data-Driven Upselling – AI-powered insights help agents recommend relevant upgrades and add-ons, ensuring upselling is value-driven and aligned with customer needs.
Sales Co-Pilot Support – We utilise co-pilots which provide real-time recommendations, guided scripts, and dynamic objection handling to enhance sales effectiveness.
Training and Quality Assurance – We invest in ongoing training, coaching, and call monitoring to ensure agents apply best practices, maintain compliance, and deliver high-quality interactions.
Continuous Optimisation – Performance analytics and feedback loops ensure continuous retention, upselling, and overall customer experience improvement.

## How do you handle customer data and ensure privacy and confidentiality?
At Firstsource, we take customer data privacy and confidentiality very seriously and have implemented robust processes to ensure compliance with data protection regulations such as GDPR and CCPA. Here are some key aspects of our approach: 
Data processing and consent: We process personal data only when at least one of the following conditions is met: the data subject has given permission, processing is necessary for the performance of a contract, compliance with a legal obligation, protection of vital interests, performance of a task in the public interest, or legitimate interests pursued by the data controller 
Records and accountability: We maintain appropriate records related to processing personal data, including Records of Processing Activities (RoPAs), inventory of personal data, Data Flow Diagrams (DFDs), and data breach records. These records are reviewed and updated regularly to ensure accountability 
Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs): DPIAs are conducted periodically for applicable processes and applications to identify and manage risks to personal data 
Security measures: We implement robust data security measures to protect customer data, including encryption, access controls, and regular security audits. Our systems are designed to ensure data confidentiality, integrity, and availability 
Compliance with regulations: We ensure compliance with data protection regulations such as GDPR and CCPA by following best practices and guidelines. This includes obtaining visitors' consent for the deployment of cookies and ensuring that personal data is processed lawfully and transparently 
Data subject rights: We respect and uphold the rights of data subjects, including the right to access, rectify, delete, restrict processing, and object to the processing of their data. We also provide transparency in how personal data is used and processed 
Incident management: In the event of a data breach or incident, we have a well-defined incident management process to promptly report and address the issue. This includes maintaining a data breach record and collaborating with relevant stakeholders to resolve the incident 
By adhering to these processes and continuously monitoring and improving our data protection practices, we ensure customer data is handled with the utmost care and confidentiality.

## General Company Information:


## What is your company's history and experience in providing customer care and telesales support?
Company Overview
Founded in 2001 as a subsidiary of ICICI Bank, Firstsource began focusing on business process outsourcing (BPO) and rapidly expanded its capabilities through strategic acquisitions in customer services. In 2006, it rebranded as Firstsource Solutions Ltd, establishing itself as a global BPO provider, and went public in 2007, listing on India's Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and National Stock Exchange (NSE). A pivotal moment came in 2012 when the RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group acquired a controlling stake, integrating Firstsource into a USD 7 billion conglomerate with diverse interests spanning power, energy, retail, FMCG, media, and sports.
Since then, Firstsource has continued to grow, with operations across the US, UK, South Africa, India, Mexico, Australia, Trinidad & Tobago, Romania, Turkey, and Philippines, serving clients from key industries such as Telecom and Media, Healthcare, Banking and Finance, and Retail. As of 2024, Firstsource employs over 32,000 professionals and is recognised by the industry as a leader in digital customer service solutions, dedicated to delivering seamless, omnichannel experiences. Some of our recent recognitions include:
Quadrant SPARK Matrix™ ranked us as a Leader in Contact Center Outsourcing Services in 2023.
In the ISG Provider Lens™ Study 2023, we were recognised as a Leader in Europe, Global, and the US for Customer Experience Services.
The Everest Group PEAK Matrix® 2023 positioned us as Major Contenders in EMEA and Americas for Customer Experience Management (CXM) Services.
Avasant’s 2023-2024 RadarView™ labelled us as Disruptors in Contact Center Business Process Transformation.
NelsonHall’s CX Services Transformation NEAT Results ranked us as Leaders in Cost Optimisation and Revenue Generation Capability.
Customer service and telesales experience 
Firstsource is a trusted partner for leading telecom providers, delivering high-quality customer service and telesales solutions that drive customer satisfaction, revenue growth, and operational efficiencies. With extensive experience and 8,000+ FTEs supporting MVNOs and Tier-1 telecom brands, we understand evolving customer expectations and industry challenges, helping our clients stay competitive.

For peak hour staffing needs, managers utilise dedicated employees who are available but not scheduled to work (often called ‘jumpers’). They will immediately log on to take calls. 
Onsite agents, team leaders, and quality analysts are needed to manage sudden volume spikes.

Shrinkage
In the context of customer service, Workforce Management (WFM) plays a vital role in aligning customer demand with the labour supply. A key aspect of WFM is the management of shrinkage, which refers to the portion of work hours where staff are on the clock but not directly engaged in customer interactions. This includes time allocated for breaks, training sessions, team meetings, and other non-call activities.

Detailed recruitment process steps:
Step-1: HR screening
After calibration, the recruiter begins screening profiles received against the JD and calibration inputs to shortlist candidates. Post-screening, the recruiter speaks to the candidates to validate the details mentioned in the resumé. Selected resumés by the recruiter are put forward for further rounds.
Step-2: Preliminary screening
The next step is a preliminary check of the candidate’s communication skills. This is done through:
Voice support screening: The HR team conducts an initial screening round, termed Free Speech Activity (FSA), to comprehensively assess each candidate's skills, experience, and overall fit for the role. 
Messaging support screening: Typing test and conversational/situational writing is our initial screening methodology for instant messaging processes. 
Step-3: Technical assessment
Depending on the role and JD, we implement a comprehensive array of assessments to evaluate each candidate's suitability for the role thoroughly. 
Step- 4: Functional round/ Operations round
The operations/functional manager will conduct the next round of discussion. This further ascertains the candidate’s fitment in a particular role regarding skills and attitude. This round captures the remarks and final status of the candidate for evaluation. The evaluation process of this round differs based on the hiring manager's preferences.
Step-5: HR discussion
The HR discussion is conducted to evaluate a candidate on various competencies like stability, teamwork, process fitment, flexibility, and willingness to learn. The candidate is evaluated on these competencies, and the recruiter ascertains the compensation and job profile expectations. The recruiter engages in an extensive competency-based interview process with the candidate. Once a candidate clears all the above stages of selection, a final HR discussion takes place to take a final call on the candidate’s selection status. Issues related to salary, company policies, joining date, etc, are addressed, and a final decision on their selection is taken. The candidate is issued a Letter of Intent, which states that the final offer letter is conditional to the candidate, who must provide all the documents on time to the company's satisfaction. They would then receive their offer/appointment letters and be ready for onboarding.
Step-6: Background verification
After the successful completion of documentation formalities and offer acceptance on SAP SuccessFactors, the background verification is initiated for the candidate as per the client’s requirements. 
Step-7: Onboarding and induction
Depending on the date of joining assigned to the candidate, an induction is designed for the candidate to get oriented to the Firstsource environment. The induction covers the corporate overview, which gives our senior leadership members detailed insight into Firstsource’s service offerings, followed by an HR overview, which talks about performance, talent management, policies and processes, and various tools employees use daily.
As mentioned, we have immense experience in sourcing and recruiting the right profiles for Telecom and Media companies like Lyca. Our recruiters are experienced in selecting the right personas with the requisite skill sets, aptitude, and attitude to imbibe Lyca's culture and values.

Quality check methodology
Based on the client's needs and regulatory requirements, our QA team will adopt multiple approaches to ensure all clients achieve their desired business goals. Precision monitoring: This is conducted weekly to check adherence to behavioural and regulatory metrics highlighting errors. Another integral part of the quality assurance methodology at Firstsource is the calibration process. This process ensures consistency among evaluators and alignment with client requirements.
Regular calibration sessions ensure evaluations align with the client’s expectations. The following are the two types of calibration we carry out:
Internal calibration - a weekly exercise conducted by the quality leads to align and ensure consistency between the quality, training and operational teams. This weekly variation would be captured, reported, and actions taken as necessary
Client calibration – the calibration frequency depends on client availability. However, an exercise is conducted in conjunction between internal quality leads and relevant client parties to align and ensure consistency in quality expectations
Feedback and coaching:
Team Leaders provide agents with call-related feedback. Two types of feedback are provided: red alerts for compliance or customer-impacting errors and coaching attributes such as communication or process errors that impact the customer.
Feedback and alert process - A red flag may be identified throughout the quality checking process and a failure across compliance, process, and behaviours.
Should a red flag be highlighted, the following steps are taken:
All details are stored in a central location to allow trend/gap analysis to be completed to ensure people are managed accordingly, communicated effectively and provided with the necessary training/coaching to close knowledge gaps
Agents are notified in real-time by the QC team through a notification email which goes directly to the Agent, Team Leader and Operations Manager
Feedback will be delivered, and the corrective action will be completed per the Firstsource consequence management policy. However, as an additional step to ensure the Agent fully understands the process, they will complete a knowledge base module followed by a test to ensure understanding. The results are shared with the quality team, a follow-up check is completed, and the issue has been fully rectified. Depending on the severity of the failure, the Agent could potentially be removed from any further activity
Feedback/coaching agents who have achieved an insufficient QA score on a singular occasion:
The QA team completes monitoring and includes details about how an agent managed the interaction. This is broken down to specify and highlight customer experience /soft skills, procedures, system actions, and compliance. The focus areas are identified and specific to the type of contact monitored, outlining how to overcome the gaps or misses.
This information is shared with TL, who then coaches the agent on the focus areas highlighted.
The QA team checks for coaching adherence, followed by coaching retention through a dip check on the focus areas for the agent. The following week, the QA team picks a similar interaction to monitor to gauge the effectiveness of coaching done by TLs.

## Legal and Compliance:


## Do you have experience with the legal and compliance requirements for customer support and telesales in our region?
Firstsource is a global company known for its telesales and customer support industry clients. We have extensive experience with legal and compliance requirements, providing solutions that ensure regional regulation adherence and improve customer experience. ## Can you provide details on your insurance coverage and liability protection?
Firstsource offers comprehensive insurance coverage and liability protection to ensure the safety and security of its operations while servicing clients worldwide. Please see the liability insurance details below for your reference.


## How do you handle customer data and ensure privacy and confidentiality?
At Firstsource, we take customer data privacy and confidentiality very seriously and have implemented robust processes to ensure compliance with data protection regulations such as GDPR and CCPA. Here are some key aspects of our approach: 
Data processing and consent: We process personal data only when at least one of the following conditions is met: the data subject has given permission, processing is necessary for the performance of a contract, compliance with a legal obligation, protection of vital interests, performance of a task in the public interest, or legitimate interests pursued by the data controller 
Records and accountability: We maintain appropriate records related to processing personal data, including Records of Processing Activities (RoPAs), inventory of personal data, Data Flow Diagrams (DFDs), and data breach records. These records are reviewed and updated regularly to ensure accountability 
Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs): DPIAs are conducted periodically for applicable processes and applications to identify and manage risks to personal data 
Security measures: We implement robust data security measures to protect customer data, including encryption, access controls, and regular security audits. Our systems are designed to ensure data confidentiality, integrity, and availability 
Compliance with regulations: We ensure compliance with data protection regulations such as GDPR and CCPA by following best practices and guidelines. This includes obtaining visitors' consent for the deployment of cookies and ensuring that personal data is processed lawfully and transparently 
Data subject rights: We respect and uphold the rights of data subjects, including the right to access, rectify, delete, restrict processing, and object to the processing of their data. We also provide transparency in how personal data is used and processed 
Incident management: In the event of a data breach or incident, we have a well-defined incident management process to promptly report and address the issue. This includes maintaining a data breach record and collaborating with relevant stakeholders to resolve the incident 
By adhering to these processes and continuously monitoring and improving our data protection practices, we ensure customer data is handled with the utmost care and confidentiality.

input: Compare Firstsource’s Re-imagine, Re-build, and Re-boot pillars in its AI-first CX transformation.
expected_output:
Firstsource’s AI-first CX transformation is structured around three pillars:

- **Re-imagine**: Focuses on redesigning CX at the front end by creating detailed customer personas, defining omnichannel journeys, designing service processes tied to customer metrics, applying industry/process standards, and driving process re-engineering and optimization.

- **Re-build**: Focuses on the technology and operating foundation, with a **cloud-first/platform-based technology blueprint**, optimized for scale and using **best-of-breed AI solutions**. It supports rebuilding the CX ecosystem to enable transformed operations.

- **Re-boot**: Focuses on operational execution using AI. This includes **AI-first CX operations**, **AI-empowered agents**, agent proficiency models/scorecards/skills management, and a **location-less operations toolkit and playbook**. It is aimed at delivering next-gen CX outcomes in day-to-day service delivery.

In short: **Re-imagine = redesign the experience**, **Re-build = create the tech foundation**, and **Re-boot = operationalize with AI-enabled delivery**.

input: Compare Firstsource’s vendor-agnostic orchestration model with single-vendor lock-in, incl. swappable STT/TTS/LLM and owned governance layers.
expected_output:
Firstsource’s orchestration model is designed to avoid single-vendor lock-in. It owns the call-flow design, compliance scripting, prompt engineering, governance, QA, and orchestration layers, while keeping underlying STT, TTS, and LLM components interchangeable. That means US Bank can standardize on preferred providers and swap components without re-platforming or rebuilding call flows.

By contrast, a single-vendor model ties the voice experience, AI models, and control layers to one provider’s roadmap, tooling, and constraints, which can increase dependency and reduce flexibility. Firstsource’s approach also avoids a proprietary “black box” platform by exposing standard integrations, webhooks, and event streams, while preserving governance and compliance controls independently of the underlying AI vendors.
context:
SourcePoint | Summary of Voice AI Capabilities, Voice Platform, Compliance/Controls etc. |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
Top strengths |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
Collections grade agentic voice capability built and proven across Firstsource's regulated financial services portfolio (Klarna , AMEX agentic AI program, Robinhood voicebot deployment). Asset class agnostic core that transfers to Auto, Mortgage, and Consumer Loan voice use cases without re-platforming. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
Vendor agnostic orchestration model. Firstsource owns the call flow design, compliance scripting, prompt engineering, governance, and QA layers  STT/TTS/LLM components are interchangeable, eliminating single-vendor lock-in and enabling US Bank to standardize on its preferred underlying providers. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
Mature governance and compliance posture purpose-built for regulated lending: relAI (Responsible & Ethical AI) framework, OWASP LLM Top 10 / MITRE ATLAS-aligned UAT (88+ test cases including prompt injection, jailbreak, context-flooding red team scenarios), DPIA, bias testing SOP, model lifecycle controls, and incident response, all already cleared through a large FinTech and AMEX GenAI control assessments. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
Top weaknesses |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
No mortgage specific voice AI deployment in production today. Our agentic voice capability is collections and servicing-proven across cards, BNPL, and consumer credit; mortgage specific call flows, intent libraries, and regulatory overlays (RESPA, TILA, CFPB mortgage servicing rules) would be built during the POV. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
Production scale is concentrated in collections and post-charge-off use cases rather than high-volume inbound servicing. Front-end servicing voice (payments, escrow, statement, payoff, hardship) is supported by capability but would benefit from a structured POV to validate containment and CSAT at US Bank's volumes.
Production timeline depends on US Bank's telephony, CRM, servicing platform (e.g., Black Knight MSP / Sagent / ICE), and authentication architecture. Integration discovery is required before committing to launch dates,  we will scope this in week one of the POV rather than preposition commitments we cannot stand behind. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
Category | Sourcepoint details |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
Quality of Real-Time Voice Experience | Firstsource operates a vendor agnostic agentic voice stack: best of breed STT (e.g., Deepgram, Google, Azure), neural TTS (ElevenLabs), and LLM (Claude, GPT-4 class) selected per use case based on accuracy, latency, and cost. E2E response latency targets sub-1.5s for conversational turns; barge-in, interruption handling, and silence/timeout management are tuned per call flow rather than left at vendor defaults.

We have benchmarked STT word error rate against accented and noisy contact-center audio across multiple deployments and tune dictionaries (loan terminology, payment terms, address formats) per client. The Klarna pilot (~4,400 inbound calls, April 2026) validated real-world conversational quality at scale, including a collaborative human-AI model that materially outperformed solo-AI and control groups on liquidation.

What we will validate in the POV: STT accuracy on US Bank's specific call audio profile, TTS voice selection and brand alignment, latency under US Bank's telephony path, and turn-taking quality on payment, escrow, and account servicing flows. |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
Architecture & Integration Fit | Architecture is modular and built around an orchestration layer that Firstsource owns. Standard integrations include: telephony/CaaS (TCN, LiveVox and Twilio), CRM and servicing platforms via REST/SOAP APIs, IVR fallback and warm transfer to human agents, authentication systems (knowledge-based or OTP) and downstream workflow/case management.

For mortgage specifically, integration to systems of record such as Black Knight MSP, Sagent, ICE Mortgage Technology, or proprietary servicing platforms is achieved via API or middleware to be confirmed against US Bank's environment in POV discovery. Data residency, cloud preferences (AWS / Azure /hybrid), and on-prem requirements are accommodated; we do not require US Bank to adopt a specific cloud or platform.

The orchestration layer exposes standard webhooks and event streams for real time analytics, supervisor monitoring, and downstream automation. No proprietary 'black box' platform is required  components can be swapped without re-implementing call flows. |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
Governance / Security / Compliance Readiness | Governance is the area where Firstsource is most mature and most differentiated. Our relAI (Responsible & Ethical AI) framework is operationalized as a nine-document control suite: AI policy, risk framework, model lifecycle SOP, compliance matrix, incident response plan, bias testing protocol, DPIA, vendor addendum, and client-facing summary.

Security and compliance posture: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, encryption in transit and at rest, role-based access, full call/transcript logging with retention controls, PII masking, and configurable zero-data-retention modes for LLM components. Adversarial and red-team testing is institutionalized  our UAT framework includes 88+ test cases mapped to OWASP LLM Top 10 and MITRE ATLAS, covering prompt injection, jailbreak, context flooding, and multi-vector attack scenarios.

Regulatory coverage relevant to US Bank's portfolio: FDCPA, TCPA, Regulation F, UDAAP, FCRA, ECOA; for mortgage specifically RESPA, TILA, CFPB mortgage servicing rules, and state-level overlays. We have completed enterprise GenAI control assessments for Bank of America and American Express, and responded to Robinhood's security questionnaire for our voicebot — these artifacts are available to accelerate US Bank's third-party review and internal model risk approval. |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
Business Fit for Banking Voice Engagement | Firstsource's domain depth in regulated lending is the core of our value proposition. Across the AMEX, Klarna, Afterpay,  and Robinhood programs we operate voice journeys covering authentication, account servicing, payment taking, payment plan negotiation, hardship handling, and compliant escalation to human agents.

For Phil's portfolio (Auto, Mortgage, Consumer Loans), the relevant call drivers payment-taking, payoff quotes, statement and balance inquiries, escrow and tax-related questions, hardship and loss mitigation triage, late stage collections, and compliant disclosure scripting  are directly addressable by our existing capability with asset-class-specific tuning. Mini-Miranda, right-party-contact verification, consent capture, opt-outs, and call recording disclosures are built-in rather than bolted on.

Our orientation is containment with a confident escalation path: AI handles what it should handle, escalates cleanly to human agents on complex, sensitive, or out-of-scope interactions, and the human-AI collaborative model (proven in the Klarna pilot) outperforms either-or approaches. |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
Operational Tooling & Supportability | Operations are supported by a combination of platform native dashboards and Firstsource built analytics layers. Standard tooling includes: real time conversation monitoring, full transcript and audio retention, intent and outcome tagging, KPI dashboards (containment, AHT, CSAT, RPC, PTP, payment conversion), call-quality scorecards, and conversation-level root-cause analysis.

Change management: prompt and call flow changes go through a controlled lifecycle (dev → UAT → production) with versioning, rollback, and red-team regression testing before promotion. A/B and shadow-mode deployment is supported so US Bank can validate changes against live traffic before full cutover.

Operating model: Firstsource provides a dedicated AI ops team (prompt engineers, conversation designers, QA analysts, compliance reviewers) plus business user facing tooling so US Bank's own teams can review transcripts, raise change requests, and monitor performance without depending on Firstsource for every adjustment. |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
Implementation Complexity & Vendor Dependency | POV path (recommended): a 60–90 day proof of value scoped to one asset class and 2–3 high-volume call drivers. Week 1–2: discovery, telephony and systems-of-record integration design, compliance script approval. Week 3–6: build, internal red-team and compliance testing. Week 7–10: shadow mode and limited live traffic. Week 11–12: scale decision and production hardening.

Implementation effort is concentrated in three areas: (1) integration to US Bank's telephony, CRM, and servicing platforms effort scales with the number of systems and the maturity of their APIs; (2) call-flow and prompt design specific to US Bank's policies, scripts, and compliance posture; (3) UAT and model-risk approval, where our existing control documentation accelerates the cycle.

Vendor dependency is deliberately constrained. Because Firstsource owns the orchestration, prompt library, and governance artifacts — and because underlying STT/TTS/LLM components are swappable — US Bank does not become locked into a single AI vendor's roadmap. Internal US Bank teams can be enabled to operate the platform over time if that is the preferred operating model. |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
Production Maturity vs Demo Quality | Honest framing: our agentic voice capability is production-deployed in collections and servicing use cases across regulated financial services   not yet at scale in mortgage specifically. Production references include the AMEX agentic AI program (under active governance review and outbound voice), Klarna's pilot (4,400 inbound calls, April 2026, with measurable liquidation lift in the human-AI collaborative model), and the Robinhood voicebot deployment (security and compliance cleared).

What is generally available today vs. what is roadmap: STT/TTS/LLM orchestration, compliance scripting, governance documentation, UAT and red-team frameworks, monitoring and analytics  all GA. Mortgage-specific intent libraries, RESPA/TILA tuned scripting, and integrations to specific mortgage servicing platforms  to be built or extended during the POV based on US Bank's environment.

We will not represent demo capability as production capability. The POV is structured precisely to give US Bank evidence under its own conditions — telephony, audio profile, customer base, call drivers — before any scale commitment is made. |  |  |  |  |  |  |

High Level Evaluation Criteria |  |  |  |

input: Based on ctx, cite 1 top weakness in Firstsource's mortgage-specific voice AI, incl. POV need.
expected_output: One top weakness is that Firstsource does not have a mortgage-specific voice AI deployment in production today. While its agentic voice capability is proven in collections and servicing across cards, BNPL, and consumer credit, mortgage-specific call flows, intent libraries, and regulatory overlays like RESPA, TILA, and CFPB mortgage servicing rules would need to be built and validated during a POV.

SourcePoint | Summary of Voice AI Capabilities, Voice Platform, Compliance/Controls etc. |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
Top strengths |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
Collections grade agentic voice capability built and proven across Firstsource's regulated financial services portfolio (Klarna , AMEX agentic AI program, Robinhood voicebot deployment). Asset class agnostic core that transfers to Auto, Mortgage, and Consumer Loan voice use cases without re-platforming. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
Vendor agnostic orchestration model.
